Solve by elimination: $$\begin{cases}5x+2y=6\\3x-10y=26\end{cases}.$$
Solve by elimination: $$\begin{cases}2x-y=12\\6x+2y=21\end{cases}.$$
Solve by elimination: $$\begin{cases}3x-2y=-6\\6x+3y=2\end{cases}.$$
Solve by elimination: $$\begin{cases}3x+8y=33\\6x=3+5y\end{cases}.$$
Solve by substitution: $$\begin{cases}x+3y=11\\4x-7y=6\end{cases}.$$

Solve by substitution: $$\begin{cases}2y=2x-3\\3y=x-1\end{cases}.$$
Solve $$\begin{cases}3x-2y=5\\5(x+y)=6(x+1)\end{cases}.$$
Solve $$\begin{cases}x-\tfrac{2y}{3}=4\\2x+3y+4=0\end{cases}.$$
Solve $$\begin{cases}3y=5(x-2)\\3(x-1)+y+4=0\end{cases}.$$
Given $$\begin{cases}3x+ky=8\\x-2ky=5\end{cases}$$, (a) show $$x=3$$ for any $$k\ne0$$.
Chapter 3-Equations and inequal.solution_text: From second $$x=5+2ky$$; sub into first $$3(5+2ky)+ky=8\Rightarrow15+7ky=8\Rightarrow y=-\tfrac{1}{k},\ x=3.$$

Chapter 3-Equations and inequal.question_text: (b) Given also $$y=\tfrac12$$, find $$k$$.
The system $$\begin{cases}2x-py=5\\4x+5y+q=0\end{cases}$$ has $$x=q,\ y=-1.$$ Find $$p,q$$.
Chapter 3-Equations and inequal.solution_text: From first $$2q+p=5$$, from second $$5q-5=0\Rightarrow q=1,\ p=3.$$

Chapter 3-Equations and inequal.question_text: Solve the simultaneous equations: $$\begin{cases}x+y=11\\xy=30\end{cases}.$$

Find the intersection points of $$y=3x-1$$ with the curve $$y^2=xy+15$$.
Chapter 3-Equations and inequal.hint: Substitute $$y=3x-1$$ and solve the quadratic in $$x$$.

Given $$x^2+8kx+k=0$$ has equal roots, find $$k$$ (with $$k\ne0$$).

Chapter 3-Equations and inequal.question_text: Use set notation to describe all $$x$$ such that $$3(x-2)>x-4$$ and $$4x+12>2x+17$$.
Chapter 3-Equations and inequal.hint: Solve each inequality, then intersect the solutions.
Chapter 3-Equations and inequal.solution_text: From $$3x-6>x-4\Rightarrow2x>2\Rightarrow x>1$$ and $$4x+12>2x+17\Rightarrow2x>5\Rightarrow x>\tfrac{5}{2}$$; intersection: $$\{x\mid x>\tfrac{5}{2}\}=(\tfrac{5}{2},\infty).$$

Chapter 3-Equations and inequal.question_text: Use set notation to describe all $$x$$ such that $$2x-5<x-1$$ and $$7(x+1)>23-x$$.
Use set notation to describe all $$x$$ such that $$2x-3\ge2$$ and $$3(x+2)<12+x$$.
Chapter 3-Equations and inequal.solution_text: First $$2x\ge5\Rightarrow x\ge\tfrac{5}{2}$$; second $$3x+6<12+x\Rightarrow2x<6\Rightarrow x<3$$; intersection: $$\{x\mid \tfrac{5}{2}\le x<3\}=[\tfrac{5}{2},3).$$

Chapter 3-Equations and inequal.question_text: Use set notation to describe all $$x$$ such that $$15-x<2(11-x)$$ and $$5(3x-1)\ge12x+19$$.
Chapter 3-Equations and inequal.solution_text: First $$15-x<22-2x\Rightarrow x<7$$; second $$15x-5\ge12x+19\Rightarrow3x\ge24\Rightarrow x\ge8$$; intersection is $$\varnothing$$ (no real $$x$$).

Chapter 3-Equations and inequal.question_text: Use set notation to describe all $$x$$ such that $$3x+8\le20$$ and $$2(3x-7)\ge x+6$$.
Chapter 3-Equations and inequal.solution_text: First $$3x\le12\Rightarrow x\le4$$; second $$6x-14\ge x+6\Rightarrow5x\ge20\Rightarrow x\ge4$$; intersection: $$\{4\}.$$

Chapter 3-Equations and inequal.question_text: Use set notation to describe all $$x$$ such that $$5x+3<9$$ or $$5(2x+1)>27$$.
Use set notation to describe all $$x$$ such that $$4(3x+7)\le20$$ or $$2(3x-5)\ge\frac{7-6x}{2}$$.
Given $$A=\{x:3x+5>2\},\ B=\{x:\tfrac{x}{2}+1\le3\},\ C=\{x:11<2x-1\}$$ and $$A\cap(B\cup C)=\{x:p<x\le q\}\cup\{x:x>r\}$$, find $$p,q,r$$.
Chapter 3-Equations and inequal.hint: Find each set, then compute $$B\cup C$$ and intersect with $$A$$.
Chapter 3-Equations and inequal.solution_text: $$A=(-1,\infty),\ B=(-\infty,4],\ C=(6,\infty)$$ so $$B\cup C=(-\infty,4]\cup(6,\infty).$$ Then $$A\cap(B\cup C)=(-1,4]\cup(6,\infty).$$ Hence $$p=-1,\ q=4,\ r=6.$$

Chapter 3-Equations and inequal.question_text: Use set notation to describe $$x$$ such that $$x^2-7x+10<0$$ and $$3x+5\le17.$$
Use set notation to describe $$x$$ such that $$x^2-x-6>0$$ and $$10-2x<5.$$
Use set notation to describe $$x$$ such that $$4x^2-3x-1<0$$ and $$4(x+2)<15-(x+7).$$
Use set notation to describe $$x$$ such that $$x^2-x-1<0$$ and $$14\le3x-2.$$
Use set notation to describe $$x$$ such that $$x^2-x-12>0$$ and $$3x+17>2.$$
Use set notation to describe $$x$$ such that $$x^2-2x-3<0$$ and $$x^2-3x+2>0.$$
Find the set of values of x (x≠0) for which $$\frac{2}{x}<1.$$
Chapter 3-Equations and inequal.hint: Multiply by x² and consider sign of x.
Chapter 3-Equations and inequal.solution_text: For x>0: 2<x ⇒ x>2; for x<0: 2>x ⇒ x<0; hence \boxed{x<0\text{ or }x>2}.

Chapter 3-Equations and inequal.question_text: Find the set of values of x (x≠0) for which $$5>\frac{4}{x}.$$
Chapter 3-Equations and inequal.hint: Multiply both sides by x (consider sign).
Chapter 3-Equations and inequal.solution_text: For x>0: 5x>4⇒x>\tfrac45; for x<0: 5x<4⇒x<\tfrac45 (always true for x<0). Hence \boxed{x<0\text{ or }x>\tfrac45}.

Chapter 3-Equations and inequal.question_text: Find the set of values of x (x≠0) for which $$\frac{1}{x}+3>2.$$
Chapter 3-Equations and inequal.solution_text: For x>0: 1>-x ⇒ always true; for x<0: multiply gives 1<-x ⇒ x<-1. Hence \boxed{x>0\text{ or }x<-1}.

Chapter 3-Equations and inequal.question_text: Find the set of values of x (x≠0) for which $$6+\frac{5}{x}\ge\frac{8}{x}.$$
Chapter 3-Equations and inequal.solution_text: For x>0: 6x≥3⇒x≥\tfrac12; for x<0: 6x≤3⇒x≤\tfrac12 (always true for x<0). Hence \boxed{x<0\text{ or }x\ge\tfrac12}.

Chapter 3-Equations and inequal.question_text: Find the set of values of x (x≠0) for which $$25>\frac{1}{x^2}.$$
Find the set of values of x (x≠0) for which $$\frac{6}{x^2}+\frac{7}{x}\le3.$$
Chapter 3-Equations and inequal.hint: Multiply by x² and solve quadratic inequality.

Chapter 3-Equations and inequal.question_text: Find the range of k for which $$x^2-kx+(k+3)=0$$ has no real roots.
Find the range of p for which $$px^2+px-2=0$$ has real roots.
Find the set of values of x for which $$x^2-5x-14>0.$$
Find the set of x for which $$2(3x-1)<4-3x.$$
Find the set of x for which $$2x^2-5x-3<0.$$
Chapter 3-Equations and inequal.hint: Find roots and take between interval.

Chapter 3-Equations and inequal.question_text: Find the set of x for which both $$2(3x-1)<4-3x$$ and $$2x^2-5x-3<0.$$
Find the set of values of x (x≠3) for which $$\frac{5}{x-3}<2.$$
Chapter 3-Equations and inequal.solution_text: $$5<2(x-3)\Rightarrow x>5.5$$ when x>3; and $$5>2(x-3)\Rightarrow x<0.5$$ when x<3; hence \boxed{x<\tfrac12\text{ or }x>\tfrac{11}{2}}.$$

Chapter 3-Equations and inequal.question_text: For $$k x^2 - 2kx + 3 = 0$$, prove that it has no real roots when $$0\le k<3.$$
For the simultaneous equations $$2kx - y = 4$$ and $$4kx + 3y = -2,$$ where k is a constant, (a) Show that y = –2. (b) Find x in terms of k.
Chapter 3-Equations and inequal.hint: Use elimination: multiply first equation by 3 and add to second.

Chapter 3-Equations and inequal.question_text: Solve the equations $$x + 2y = 3$$ and $$x^2 - 4y^2 = -33.$$
Given $$x-2y=1$$ and $$3xy-y^2=8,$$ (a) Show that $$5y^2+3y-8=0.$$ (b) Find all pairs (x,y).
Chapter 3-Equations and inequal.hint: Use substitution $$x=2y+1$$ into the second equation.

Chapter 3-Equations and inequal.question_text: By eliminating y from $$x+y=2$$ and $$x^2+xy-y^2=-1,$$ (a) show that $$x^2-6x+3=0$$. (b) Hence solve for x and y, giving results in the form $$a\pm b\sqrt6.$$
(a) Given that $$3^x = 9^{y-1},$$ show that $$x = 2y - 2.$$ (b) Solve the simultaneous equations $$x = 2y - 2$$ and $$x^2 = y^2 + 7.$$
Chapter 3-Equations and inequal.hint: Use properties of indices and substitution.
Chapter 3-Equations and inequal.solution_text: (a) $$9^{y-1}=(3^2)^{y-1}=3^{2y-2}\Rightarrow x=2y-2.$$ (b) Substitute into second: $$(2y-2)^2=y^2+7\Rightarrow3y^2-8y-3=0\Rightarrow y=3,-\tfrac13,$$ hence $$x=4,-\tfrac83.$$ \boxed{(x,y)=(4,3),(-\tfrac83,-\tfrac13)}.

Chapter 3-Equations and inequal.question_text: (b) Solve the simultaneous equations $$x+2y=3$$ and $$x^2-2y+4y^2=18.$$
Chapter 3-Equations and inequal.hint: Substitute $$x=3-2y$$ and simplify to quadratic in y.

Chapter 4-Graphs and transforma.hint: Start by writing the equation in the form $$y=(x-p)(x-q)(x-r)$$ using the x-intercepts.

Chapter 4-Graphs and transforma.question_text: The graph of $$y=ax^3+bx^2+cx+d$$ is shown opposite, where $$a,b,c,d$$ are real constants. Find the values of $$a,b,c,d$$.
Chapter 4-Graphs and transforma.hint: Use factor form from x-intercepts (touching point is a repeated root), then use the y-intercept to find $$a$$.
Chapter 4-Graphs and transforma.correct_answer: $$x\text{-intercepts }-1,\ 3\text{ (double)}\Rightarrow y=a(x+1)(x-3)^2,\ y(0)=2\Rightarrow2=9a\Rightarrow a=\frac29,\ y=\frac29(x+1)(x-3)^2=\frac29x^3-\frac{10}9x^2+\frac23x+2\Rightarrow b=-\frac{10}9,\ c=\frac23,\ d=2$$

Chapter 4-Graphs and transforma.question_text: Given that $$f(x)=(x-10)(x^2-2x)+12x$$ (a) Express $$f(x)$$ in the form $$x(ax^2+bx+c)$$ where $$a,b,c$$ are real constants. (b) Hence factorise $$f(x)$$ completely. (c) Sketch the graph of $$y=f(x)$$ showing clearly the points where the graph intersects the axes.
Chapter 4-Graphs and transforma.hint: Factor out $$x$$, simplify, then factor the quadratic; x-intercepts are the axis intersections.

Chapter 4-Graphs and transforma.correct_answer: $$\Delta=25-56=-31<0\Rightarrow x^2+5x+14\text{ has no real roots};\ y=0:\ x=-5,4;\ y(0)=5(-4)(14)=-280\Rightarrow(0,-280)$$

Chapter 4-Graphs and transforma.question_text: $$\text{Use a separate diagram to sketch }y=\frac{2}{x^2}\text{ and }y=\frac{5}{x^2}.$$
Chapter 4-Graphs and transforma.hint: $$\text{For }y=\frac{k}{x^2}:\ x\ne0,\ \text{asymptotes }x=0,\ y=0,\ \text{symmetric about y-axis. If }k_2>k_1>0,\ \frac{k_2}{x^2}\text{ lies above }\frac{k_1}{x^2}.$$
Chapter 4-Graphs and transforma.correct_answer: $$\begin{aligned}\textbf{Common features (both graphs):}\\\text{Domain: }&x\ne0\\\text{Vertical asymptote: }&x=0\\\text{Horizontal asymptote: }&y=0\\\text{Symmetry: }&y\text{-axis since }f(-x)=f(x)\\\text{Position: }&y>0\text{ (both above x-axis)}\\[6pt]\textbf{Key points to plot:}\\y=\frac{2}{x^2}:&(1,2),\ (2,\tfrac12),\ (-1,2),\ (-2,\tfrac12)\\y=\frac{5}{x^2}:&(1,5),\ (2,\tfrac54),\ (-1,5),\ (-2,\tfrac54)\\[6pt]\textbf{Relative position:}\\\frac{5}{x^2}&>\frac{2}{x^2}\ \text{for all }x\ne0\\\Rightarrow\ y=\frac{5}{x^2}&\text{ is always above }y=\frac{2}{x^2}.\\[6pt]\text{Draw two upward-opening reciprocal-squared branches in quadrants I and II approaching }x=0\text{ and }y=0,\ \text{and label each curve.}\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 4-Graphs and transforma.question_text: $$\text{Use a separate diagram to sketch }y=\frac{3}{x^2}\text{ and }y=-\frac{3}{x^2}.$$
Chapter 4-Graphs and transforma.hint: $$\text{Changing the sign reflects the graph in the x-axis. Both have asymptotes }x=0,\ y=0\text{ and are symmetric about the y-axis.}$$
Chapter 4-Graphs and transforma.correct_answer: $$\begin{aligned}\textbf{Common features (both graphs):}\\\text{Domain: }&x\ne0\\\text{Vertical asymptote: }&x=0\\\text{Horizontal asymptote: }&y=0\\\text{Symmetry: }&y\text{-axis since }f(-x)=f(x)\\[6pt]\textbf{For }y=\frac{3}{x^2}:\\&k>0\Rightarrow y>0\text{ so branches are above the x-axis (quadrants I and II).}\\\text{Points: }&(1,3),\ (2,\tfrac34),\ (-1,3),\ (-2,\tfrac34)\\[6pt]\textbf{For }y=-\frac{3}{x^2}:\\&k<0\Rightarrow y<0\text{ so branches are below the x-axis (quadrants III and IV).}\\&\text{This is the reflection of }y=\frac{3}{x^2}\text{ in the x-axis.}\\\text{Points: }&(1,-3),\ (2,-\tfrac34),\ (-1,-3),\ (-2,-\tfrac34)\\[6pt]\text{Sketch both sets of branches approaching }x=0\text{ and }y=0,\ \text{and label each curve clearly.}\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 4-Graphs and transforma.question_text: $$\text{Use a separate diagram to sketch }y=-\frac{2}{x^2}\text{ and }y=-\frac{6}{x^2}.$$
Chapter 4-Graphs and transforma.hint: $$\text{Both have }k<0\Rightarrow\text{ both curves lie below the x-axis; larger }|k|\text{ gives values further down (more negative).}$$
Chapter 4-Graphs and transforma.correct_answer: $$\begin{aligned}\textbf{Common features (both graphs):}\\\text{Domain: }&x\ne0\\\text{Vertical asymptote: }&x=0\\\text{Horizontal asymptote: }&y=0\\\text{Symmetry: }&y\text{-axis since }f(-x)=f(x)\\\text{Position: }&y<0\text{ (both below x-axis, in quadrants III and IV)}\\[6pt]\textbf{Key points to plot:}\\y=-\frac{2}{x^2}:&(1,-2),\ (2,-\tfrac12),\ (-1,-2),\ (-2,-\tfrac12)\\y=-\frac{6}{x^2}:&(1,-6),\ (2,-\tfrac32),\ (-1,-6),\ (-2,-\tfrac32)\\[6pt]\textbf{Relative position:}\\-\frac{6}{x^2}&<-\frac{2}{x^2}\ \text{for all }x\ne0\\\Rightarrow\ y=-\frac{6}{x^2}&\text{ lies below }y=-\frac{2}{x^2}\text{ everywhere.}\\[6pt]\text{Draw two downward reciprocal-squared branches in quadrants III and IV approaching }x=0\text{ and }y=0,\ \text{and label each curve.}\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 4-Graphs and transforma.question_text: $$\text{(a) On the same axes sketch the curves }y=(x+1)^3\text{ and }y=3x(x-1).\ \text{(b) Explain how your sketch shows that there is only one real solution to }x^3+6x+1=0.$$
Chapter 4-Graphs and transforma.hint: $$\text{At intersection points }(x+1)^3=3x(x-1).\ \text{The number of real solutions equals the number of intersections.}$$
Chapter 4-Graphs and transforma.correct_answer: $$\begin{aligned}\textbf{Curve }y=(x+1)^3:&\ \text{increasing cubic for all }x\\\text{x-intercept: }(x+1)^3=0&\Rightarrow x=-1\\\text{y-intercept: }x=0&\Rightarrow y=1\\[6pt]\textbf{Curve }y=3x(x-1):&=3x^2-3x\ \text{(upward parabola)}\\\text{x-intercepts: }&x=0,\ 1\\\text{Vertex: }&x=\tfrac12,\ y=-\tfrac34\\[8pt]\textbf{Intersections:}\\(x+1)^3&=3x(x-1)\\x^3+3x^2+3x+1&=3x^2-3x\\x^3+6x+1&=0\\[6pt]\text{From the sketch, the graphs intersect once only.}\\\therefore\ \text{the equation has exactly one real solution.}\end{aligned}$$
$$f(x)=x^2-x^3,\ x^2(1-x)=0\Rightarrow x=0\text{ (double root)},1;\ y\text{-intercept }(0,0);\ \text{cubic touching x-axis at }(0,0)\text{ and crossing at }(1,0).$$
$$y=f(x+1)\text{ is the graph of }y=f(x)\text{ shifted }1\text{ unit to the left.}$$

Chapter 4-Graphs and transforma.question_text: $$\text{Sketch the curve }y=x^2+3x-4.$$ $$\text{On the same axes, sketch the graph of }5y=x^2+3x-4.$$
Chapter 4-Graphs and transforma.hint: $$5y=x^2+3x-4\Rightarrow y=\tfrac15(x^2+3x-4)\text{ is a vertical scale factor } \tfrac15\text{ of }y=x^2+3x-4.$$
Chapter 4-Graphs and transforma.correct_answer: $$y=\tfrac15(x^2+3x-4);\ \text{x-intercepts unchanged: }(-4,0),(1,0);\ \text{y-intercept: }(0,-\tfrac45);\ \text{vertex: }\left(-\tfrac32,-\tfrac54\right);\ \text{same axis of symmetry }x=-\tfrac32,\ \text{opens upward, flatter than (a).}$$

Chapter 4-Graphs and transforma.question_text: $$\text{The point }P(2,1)\text{ lies on }y=f(x).\ \text{On the graph of }y=af(x),\ P\text{ maps to }Q(4,1).\ \text{Determine }a.$$
Chapter 4-Graphs and transforma.hint: $$\text{For }y=af(x),\ x\text{ stays the same and }y\text{ is multiplied by }a.$$
Chapter 4-Graphs and transforma.correct_answer: $$\text{Under }y=af(x),\ (x,y)\mapsto(x,ay).\ \text{So }P(2,1)\mapsto(2,a).\ \text{Given image is }Q(4,1)\text{ (same y as original), this indicates a horizontal stretch by factor }2\text{, i.e. }y=f\!\left(\tfrac{x}{2}\right).\ \text{But if the intended transformation is }y=af(x)\text{ then }x\text{ cannot change, so the only consistent value is }a=1.$$

Chapter 4-Graphs and transforma.question_title: Image of P under given transformations
Chapter 4-Graphs and transforma.question_text: $$\text{Write down the coordinates of the point to which }P(2,1)\text{ maps under: (i) }f(x-4)\ \text{(ii) }3f(x)\ \text{(iii) }\tfrac15 f(x)-4.$$
$$\text{The diagram shows the curve }y=5+2x-x^2\text{ and the line }y=2.\ \text{The curve and the line intersect at points }A\text{ and }B.\ \text{Find the x-coordinates of }A\text{ and }B.$$
Chapter 4-Graphs and transforma.hint: $$\text{At points of intersection, set the equations equal: }5+2x-x^2=2.$$
Chapter 4-Graphs and transforma.correct_answer: $$\begin{aligned}5+2x-x^2&=2\\-x^2+2x+3&=0\\x^2-2x-3&=0\\(x-3)(x+1)&=0\\x&=3\ \text{or}\ x=-1\\\therefore\ \text{The x-coordinates of }A\text{ and }B\text{ are }-1\text{ and }3.\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: $$m=\frac{7-(2t+1)}{3t-t};\ \text{then }c=y-mx.$$
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: $$m=\frac{6-2t}{2t}=\frac{3-t}{t}\ (t\neq0).$$ $$c=(2t+1)-m t=2t+1-(3-t)=3t-2.$$ $$\boxed{m=\frac{3-t}{t},\ c=3t-2.}$$ $$\text{Vertical when }t=0\ (\text{since }A=B=(0,1)\text{ gives undefined slope}).$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: $$A(1,2),\ B(9,6).$$ Point $$C(x,y)$$ is such that the midpoint of $$AC$$ lies on the line $$y=x-1$$ and $$C$$ lies on $$AB$$. Find $$C.$$
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: $$\text{Find equation of }AB;\ C\text{ on }AB.\ \text{Midpoint condition gives another equation.}$$
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: $$AB:\ m=\frac{6-2}{9-1}=\frac12\Rightarrow y-2=\frac12(x-1)\Rightarrow y=\frac12x+\frac32.$$ $$\text{Midpoint of }AC:\ \left(\frac{1+x}{2},\frac{2+y}{2}\right)\text{ lies on }y=x-1.$$ $$\frac{2+y}{2}=\frac{1+x}{2}-1\Rightarrow y=x-3.$$ Solve with $$y=\frac12x+\frac32\Rightarrow x-3=\frac12x+\frac32\Rightarrow x=9,\ y=6.$$ $$\boxed{C(9,6)}.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_title: Line through a point with fixed intercept product
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: $$\text{A line passes through }(2,3)\text{ and cuts the axes at }(p,0)\text{ and }(0,q)\text{ with }pq=12.\ \text{Find the possible equations.}$$
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: $$\text{Use intercept form }\frac{x}{p}+\frac{y}{q}=1\text{ and }pq=12.$$
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: $$\frac{x}{p}+\frac{y}{q}=1,\ pq=12\Rightarrow q=\frac{12}{p}.$$ $$\frac{x}{p}+\frac{yp}{12}=1.$$ Substitute $(2,3)$: $$\frac{2}{p}+\frac{3p}{12}=1\Rightarrow \frac{2}{p}+\frac{p}{4}=1.$$ Multiply by $4p$: $$8+p^2=4p\Rightarrow p^2-4p+8=0,$$ discriminant $=16-32<0$ ⇒ no real solutions. $$\boxed{\text{No such real line exists.}}$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: For $$r$$: $$m_r=\frac{8-4}{6-1}=\frac45.$$ For $$s$$: $$m_s=\frac{9-(-3)}{20-5}=\frac{12}{15}=\frac45.$$ Since $$m_r=m_s,$$ the lines are parallel.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The coordinates of quadrilateral $$ABCD$$ are $$A(-6,2),\ B(4,8),\ C(6,1),\ D(-9,-8).$$ Show that the quadrilateral is a trapezium.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: A trapezium has exactly one pair of parallel sides.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Gradient $$AB=\frac{8-2}{4-(-6)}=\frac{6}{10}=\frac35.$$ Gradient $$CD=\frac{-8-1}{-9-6}=\frac{-9}{-15}=\frac35.$$ Gradients $$BC=\frac{1-8}{6-4}=-\frac72$$ and $$AD=\frac{-8-2}{-9+6}=\frac{10}{3}$$ are not equal. Hence only one pair of opposite sides is parallel, so $$ABCD$$ is a trapezium.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A line is parallel to the line $$y=5x+8$$ and its y-intercept is $$ (0,3) $$. Write down the equation of the line.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Parallel lines have the same gradient.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: The given line has gradient $$m=5.$$ A parallel line with y-intercept $$3$$ has equation $$y=5x+3.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A line is parallel to the line $$y=-\frac25x+1$$ and its y-intercept is $$ (0,-4) $$. Work out the equation of the line.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Write the equation using the same gradient and given intercept.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: The gradient is $$m=-\frac25.$$ Using $$y=mx+c$$ with $$c=-4$$ gives $$y=-\frac25x-4.$$ In general form: $$2x+5y+20=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A line is parallel to the line $$3x+6y+11=0$$ and its intercept on the y-axis is $$ (0,7) $$. Write down the equation of the line.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find the gradient from the given equation first.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: From $$3x+6y+11=0,$$ $$6y=-3x-11\Rightarrow y=-\frac12x-\frac{11}{6}.$$ Gradient $$m=-\frac12.$$ Using intercept $$7$$: $$y=-\frac12x+7.$$ In general form: $$x+2y-14=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A line is parallel to the line $$2x-3y-1=0$$ and passes through the point $$ (0,0) $$. Write down the equation of the line.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find the gradient, then use the origin as the intercept.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: From $$2x-3y-1=0,$$ $$-3y=-2x+1\Rightarrow y=\frac23x-\frac13.$$ Gradient $$m=\frac23.$$ Passing through origin gives $$y=\frac23x.$$ In general form: $$2x-3y=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Find an equation of the line that passes through $$(-2,7)$$ and is parallel to the line $$y=4x+1$$. Write your answer in the form $$ax+by+c=0$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use the same gradient and substitute the point.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: The gradient is $$m=4.$$ Using point-slope form: $$y-7=4(x+2)\Rightarrow y=4x+15.$$ Rearranging gives $$4x-y+15=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Work out whether the lines $$y=-3x+7$$ and $$6x+2y-14=0$$ are parallel.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Write both equations in the form $$y=mx+c$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: First line has gradient $$m_1=-3.$$ Second line: $$6x+2y-14=0\Rightarrow2y=-6x+14\Rightarrow y=-3x+7,$$ so $$m_2=-3.$$ Since $$m_1=m_2,$$ the lines are parallel.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Determine whether the lines $$4y=8x-1$$ and $$2x-y+5=0$$ are parallel.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Rearrange both equations to find gradients.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: First line: $$4y=8x-1\Rightarrow y=2x-\frac14,$$ so $$m_1=2.$$ Second line: $$2x-y+5=0\Rightarrow y=2x+5,$$ so $$m_2=2.$$ Since gradients are equal, the lines are parallel.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The line $$r$$ passes through $$(-2,3)$$ and $$ (4,15) $$. The line $$s$$ passes through $$ (1,-1) $$ and $$ (7,11) $$. Show that $$r$$ and $$s$$ are parallel.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find the gradient of each line.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: For $$r$$: $$m_r=\frac{15-3}{4-(-2)}=\frac{12}{6}=2.$$ For $$s$$: $$m_s=\frac{11-(-1)}{7-1}=\frac{12}{6}=2.$$ Since gradients are equal, the lines are parallel.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The coordinates of quadrilateral $$PQRS$$ are $$P(1,2),\ Q(5,10),\ R(8,6),\ S(4,-2).$$ Show that $$PQRS$$ is a trapezium.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find gradients of opposite sides and compare.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Gradient $$PQ=\frac{10-2}{5-1}=2.$$ Gradient $$RS=\frac{-2-6}{4-8}=2.$$ Gradients $$QR=\frac{6-10}{8-5}=-\frac43$$ and $$PS=\frac{-2-2}{4-1}=-\frac43$$ are not parallel to $$PQ$$. Hence exactly one pair of opposite sides is parallel, so $$PQRS$$ is a trapezium.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A line is parallel to $$y=-4x+9$$ and has y-intercept $$ (0,-2) $$. Write down its equation.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Parallel lines have the same gradient.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: The gradient is $$m=-4.$$ Using $$y=mx+c$$ with $$c=-2$$ gives $$y=-4x-2.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A line is parallel to $$3x-2y+7=0$$ and passes through $$ (0,5) $$. Find its equation.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find gradient from the given line, then use the intercept.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: From $$3x-2y+7=0,$$ $$-2y=-3x-7\Rightarrow y=\frac32x+\frac72.$$ Gradient $$m=\frac32.$$ Using intercept $$5$$: $$y=\frac32x+5.$$ In general form: $$3x-2y+10=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A line is parallel to $$5x+y-8=0$$ and passes through the origin. Write down its equation.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find the gradient first, then use $$c=0$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: From $$5x+y-8=0,$$ $$y=-5x+8,$$ so $$m=-5.$$ Through origin gives $$y=-5x.$$ In general form: $$5x+y=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Find the equation of the line through $$ (3,-1) $$ that is parallel to $$y=\frac23x-4$$. Write your answer in $$ax+by+c=0$$ form.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use point-slope form with the same gradient.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: The gradient is $$m=\frac23.$$ Using $$y+1=\frac23(x-3)\Rightarrow y=\frac23x-3.$$ Rearranging gives $$2x-3y-9=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Work out whether the lines $$x-4y=6$$ and $$2x-8y+1=0$$ are parallel.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Write both equations in $$y=mx+c$$ form.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: First line: $$x-4y=6\Rightarrow y=\frac14x-\frac32,$$ so $$m_1=\frac14.$$ Second line: $$2x-8y+1=0\Rightarrow y=\frac14x+\frac18,$$ so $$m_2=\frac14.$$ Since gradients are equal, the lines are parallel.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A line is parallel to $$y=\frac{5}{2}x-1$$ and passes through $$ (2,3) $$. Find its equation.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use point-slope form with the given point.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The coordinates of quadrilateral $$ABCD$$ are $$A(0,1),\ B(4,9),\ C(9,7),\ D(5,-1).$$ Show that $$ABCD$$ is a trapezium.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find gradients of opposite sides.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Gradient $$AB=\frac{9-1}{4-0}=2.$$ Gradient $$CD=\frac{-1-7}{5-9}=2.$$ Other sides have different gradients, so only one pair of opposite sides is parallel. Hence $$ABCD$$ is a trapezium.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A line is parallel to $$4x-2y-6=0$$ and cuts the y-axis at $$ (0,-3) $$. Find its equation.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find gradient from the given equation first.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: From $$4x-2y-6=0,$$ $$-2y=-4x+6\Rightarrow y=2x-3.$$ Using intercept $$-3$$ gives $$y=2x-3.$$ In general form: $$2x-y-3=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Find an equation of the line through $$(-5,4)$$ that is parallel to $$y=-\frac13x+2$$. Write your answer in $$ax+by+c=0$$ form.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use the same gradient and substitute the point.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Determine whether the lines $$6y=9x+12$$ and $$3x-2y+5=0$$ are parallel.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Convert both equations to $$y=mx+c$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: First line: $$6y=9x+12\Rightarrow y=\frac32x+2,$$ so $$m_1=\frac32.$$ Second line: $$3x-2y+5=0\Rightarrow y=\frac32x+\frac52,$$ so $$m_2=\frac32.$$ Since gradients are equal, the lines are parallel.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A line is parallel to $$y=7x-3$$ and has y-intercept $$ (0,10) $$. Write down the equation of the line.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Parallel lines have equal gradients.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: The gradient is $$m=7.$$ Using intercept $$10$$ gives $$y=7x+10.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Find the equation of the line through $$ (1,-6) $$ parallel to $$2x+3y-12=0$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Write the given line in $$y=mx+c$$ form first.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: From $$2x+3y-12=0,$$ $$3y=-2x+12\Rightarrow y=-\frac23x+4.$$ Using point-slope: $$y+6=-\frac23(x-1)\Rightarrow y=-\frac23x-\frac{16}{3}.$$ In general form: $$2x+3y+16=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Work out whether the lines $$y=4x-1$$ and $$8x-2y+3=0$$ are parallel.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Rearrange the second equation to find its gradient.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: First line has gradient $$4.$$ Second line: $$8x-2y+3=0\Rightarrow -2y=-8x-3\Rightarrow y=4x+\frac32.$$ Since gradients are equal, the lines are parallel.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Determine whether the lines $$y=6x-11$$ and $$12x-2y+5=0$$ are parallel.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Rearrange both equations to find their gradients.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: First line has gradient $$m_1=6.$$ Second line: $$12x-2y+5=0\Rightarrow -2y=-12x-5\Rightarrow y=6x+\frac52,$$ so $$m_2=6.$$ Since $$m_1=m_2,$$ the lines are parallel.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A line is parallel to $$y=3x-4$$ and has y-intercept $$ (0,7) $$. Write down the equation of the line.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Parallel lines have the same gradient.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: The gradient is $$m=3.$$ Using $$y=mx+c$$ with $$c=7$$ gives $$y=3x+7.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Find the equation of the line through $$ (4,-5) $$ that is parallel to $$y=-2x+1$$. Write your answer in $$ax+by+c=0$$ form.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use point-slope form with the same gradient.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: The gradient is $$m=-2.$$ Using $$y+5=-2(x-4)\Rightarrow y=-2x+3.$$ Rearranging gives $$2x+y-3=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Work out whether the lines $$5x+y-9=0$$ and $$10x+2y+3=0$$ are parallel.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Write both equations in $$y=mx+c$$ form.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: First line: $$y=-5x+9,$$ so $$m_1=-5.$$ Second line: $$2y=-10x-3\Rightarrow y=-5x-\frac32,$$ so $$m_2=-5.$$ Since gradients are equal, the lines are parallel.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The coordinates of quadrilateral $$WXYZ$$ are $$W(-2,1),\ X(2,9),\ Y(6,7),\ Z(2,-1).$$ Show that $$WXYZ$$ is a trapezium.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: A trapezium has exactly one pair of parallel sides.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Gradient $$WX=\frac{9-1}{2-(-2)}=2.$$ Gradient $$YZ=\frac{-1-7}{2-6}=2.$$ Other sides have different gradients, so only one pair of opposite sides is parallel. Hence $$WXYZ$$ is a trapezium.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A line is parallel to $$4x-3y+6=0$$ and passes through $$ (0,-2) $$. Find its equation.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find the gradient first, then use the intercept.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: From $$4x-3y+6=0,$$ $$-3y=-4x-6\Rightarrow y=\frac43x+2.$$ Using intercept $$-2$$ gives $$y=\frac43x-2.$$ In general form: $$4x-3y-6=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A line is parallel to $$y=\frac54x-3$$ and passes through the origin. Write down the equation of the line.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Parallel lines have the same gradient and pass through $$(0,0)$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: The gradient is $$m=\frac54.$$ Through the origin gives $$y=\frac54x.$$ In general form: $$5x-4y=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Determine whether the lines $$3y=6x-9$$ and $$2x-y+4=0$$ are parallel.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Convert both equations into $$y=mx+c$$ form.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: First line: $$3y=6x-9\Rightarrow y=2x-3,$$ so $$m_1=2.$$ Second line: $$2x-y+4=0\Rightarrow y=2x+4,$$ so $$m_2=2.$$ Since $$m_1=m_2,$$ the lines are parallel.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Find an equation of the line through $$(-3,6)$$ that is parallel to $$y=\frac12x+4$$. Write your answer in $$ax+by+c=0$$ form.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use the same gradient and substitute the point.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A line is parallel to $$y=-7x+2$$ and has y-intercept $$ (0,-9) $$. Write down the equation of the line.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use $$y=mx+c$$ with the same gradient.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Work out whether the lines $$x+3y=12$$ and $$2x+6y-5=0$$ are parallel.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Write both equations in $$y=mx+c$$ form.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: First line: $$3y=-x+12\Rightarrow y=-\frac13x+4.$$ Second line: $$6y=-2x+5\Rightarrow y=-\frac13x+\frac56.$$ Gradients are equal, so the lines are parallel.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A line is parallel to $$3x+4y-8=0$$ and passes through $$ (2,-1) $$. Find its equation.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find the gradient and use point-slope form.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: From $$3x+4y-8=0,$$ $$4y=-3x+8\Rightarrow y=-\frac34x+2.$$ Using $$y+1=-\frac34(x-2)\Rightarrow y=-\frac34x+\frac12.$$ In general form: $$3x+4y-2=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Determine whether the lines $$y=9x+1$$ and $$18x-2y-7=0$$ are parallel.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Rearrange the second equation to find its gradient.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: First line has gradient $$9.$$ Second line: $$-2y=-18x+7\Rightarrow y=9x-\frac72,$$ so gradients are equal. Hence the lines are parallel.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A line is parallel to $$y=-\frac34x+6$$ and has y-intercept $$ (0,1) $$. Write down its equation.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Parallel lines have the same gradient.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Find the equation of the line through $$ (6,2) $$ that is parallel to $$y=5x-7$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Write the equation using point-slope form.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The coordinates of quadrilateral $$ABCD$$ are $$A(-1,0),\ B(3,8),\ C(7,6),\ D(3,-2).$$ Show that $$ABCD$$ is a trapezium.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Compare gradients of opposite sides.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Gradient $$AB=\frac{8-0}{3-(-1)}=2.$$ Gradient $$CD=\frac{-2-6}{3-7}=2.$$ Other sides have different gradients, so exactly one pair of opposite sides is parallel. Hence $$ABCD$$ is a trapezium.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A line is parallel to $$2x-7y+14=0$$ and cuts the y-axis at $$ (0,4) $$. Find its equation.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find gradient first, then use intercept.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: From $$2x-7y+14=0,$$ $$-7y=-2x-14\Rightarrow y=\frac27x+2.$$ Using intercept $$4$$ gives $$y=\frac27x+4.$$ In general form: $$2x-7y+28=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A line is parallel to $$y=-\frac{6}{5}x+3$$ and passes through the origin. Write down its equation.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use the same gradient with $$c=0$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: The gradient is $$m=-\frac65.$$ Through the origin gives $$y=-\frac65x.$$ In general form: $$6x+5y=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Work out whether the lines $$4x+5y=20$$ and $$8x+10y-3=0$$ are parallel.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Rearrange both equations into $$y=mx+c$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: First line: $$5y=-4x+20\Rightarrow y=-\frac45x+4.$$ Second line: $$10y=-8x+3\Rightarrow y=-\frac45x+\frac{3}{10}.$$ Gradients are equal, so the lines are parallel.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_title: Equation of a line (given gradient & point)
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use point-slope form $$y-y_1=m(x-x_1).$$
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: (a) $$y-5=2(x-2)\Rightarrow y=2x+1.$$ (b) $$y-1=3(x+2)\Rightarrow y=3x+7.$$ (c) $$y+6=-1(x-3)\Rightarrow y=-x-3.$$ (d) $$y+1=-4(x+2)\Rightarrow y=-4x-9.$$ (e) $$y-10=\frac12(x+4)\Rightarrow y=\frac12x+12.$$ (f) $$y+1=-\frac23(x+6)\Rightarrow y=-\frac23x-5.$$ (g) $$y-2a=2(x-a)\Rightarrow y=2x-2a.$$ (h) $$y-3b=-\frac12(x+2b)\Rightarrow y=-\frac12x+2b.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find gradient $$m=\frac{y_2-y_1}{x_2-x_1}$$ then use $$y-y_1=m(x-x_1).$$
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: (a) $$m=4\Rightarrow y-4=4(x-2)\Rightarrow y=4x-4.$$ (b) $$m=1\Rightarrow y-2=x\Rightarrow y=x+2.$$ (c) $$m=2\Rightarrow y=2x+4.$$ (d) $$m=4\Rightarrow y=-3+4(x-5)\Rightarrow y=4x-23.$$ (e) $$m=1\Rightarrow y=x-4.$$ (f) $$m=\tfrac12\Rightarrow y=-1+\tfrac12(x+4)\Rightarrow y=\tfrac12x+1.$$ (g) $$m=-4\Rightarrow y=-5-4(x+1)\Rightarrow y=-4x-9.$$ (h) $$m=-8\Rightarrow y=-1-8(x+4)\Rightarrow y=-8x-33.$$ (i) $$m=-\tfrac72\Rightarrow y-\tfrac52=-\tfrac72(x-\tfrac13)\Rightarrow y=-\tfrac72x+\tfrac{19}{6}.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find gradient for each pair and use $$y-y_1=m(x-x_1).$$
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: $$AB: m=1\Rightarrow y=x+2.$$ $$BC: m=-\tfrac15\Rightarrow y=-\tfrac15x-\tfrac25.$$ $$CA: m=-3\Rightarrow y=-3x+14.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The straight line $$l$$ passes through $$(a,4)$$ and $$(3a,3).$$ An equation of $$l$$ is $$x+6y+c=0.$$ Find the values of $$a$$ and $$c.$$
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Substitute both points into $$x+6y+c=0$$ to form two equations, then eliminate $$c$$ to find $$a.$$
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: For $$(a,4): a+24+c=0$$ and $$(3a,3): 3a+18+c=0.$$ Subtract → $$2a-6=0\Rightarrow a=3.$$ Substitute $$a=3$$ → $$3+24+c=0\Rightarrow c=-27.$$ Hence $$a=3, c=-27.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The straight line $$l$$ passes through $$(7a,5)$$ and $$(3a,3).$$ Its equation is $$x+by-12=0.$$ Find $$a$$ and $$b.$$
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Substitute both points into $$x+by-12=0$$, eliminate $$b$$, then solve for $$a$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: For $$(7a,5): 7a+5b-12=0,$$ and $$(3a,3): 3a+3b-12=0.$$ Subtract → $$4a+2b=0\Rightarrow b=-2a.$$ Substitute into first: $$7a+5(-2a)-12=0\Rightarrow -3a=12\Rightarrow a=-4.$$ Then $$b=8.$$ Hence $$a=-4,b=8.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find $$B(0,2)$$ then use gradient formula $$m=\frac{y_2-y_1}{x_2-x_1}.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The line $$y=3x-5$$ meets x-axis at $$M$$, and $$y=-\frac{3}{4}x+\frac{3}{2}$$ meets y-axis at $$N$$. Find the equation of the line joining $$M$$ and $$N$$ in the form $$ax+by+c=0$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find intercept points by setting $$y=0$$ or $$x=0$$, then use two-point form.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: At $$y=0,$$ $$3x-5=0\Rightarrow x=\frac{5}{3}\Rightarrow M(\frac{5}{3},0).$$ At $$x=0,$$ $$y=\frac{3}{2}\Rightarrow N(0,\frac{3}{2}).$$ Gradient $$m=\frac{\frac{3}{2}-0}{0-\frac{5}{3}}=-\frac{9}{10}.$$ Equation: $$y-0=-\frac{9}{10}(x-\frac{5}{3})\Rightarrow9x+10y-15=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The line $$y=2x-10$$ meets x-axis at $$A$$, and $$y=-2x+4$$ meets y-axis at $$B$$. Find the equation of the line joining $$A$$ and $$B$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find $$A$$ at $$y=0$$ and $$B$$ at $$x=0$$, then use two-point form.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: At $$y=0,$$ $$x=5\Rightarrow A(5,0).$$ At $$x=0,$$ $$y=4\Rightarrow B(0,4).$$ Gradient $$m=\frac{4-0}{0-5}=-\frac45.$$ Equation $$y-0=-\frac45(x-5)\Rightarrow4x+5y-20=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The line $$y=4x+5$$ meets y-axis at $$C$$, and $$y=-3x-15$$ meets x-axis at $$D$$. Find the equation of line joining $$C$$ and $$D$$ in $$ax+by+c=0$$ form.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find $$C(0,5)$$ and $$D(-5,0),$$ then use gradient formula.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Lines $$y=x-5$$ and $$y=3x-13$$ intersect at $$S$$. Point $$T(-4,2)$$. Find equation of line through $$S$$ and $$T$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find $$S$$ by solving equations, then use two-point form.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: At intersection: $$x-5=3x-13\Rightarrow x=4,y=-1\Rightarrow S(4,-1).$$ Gradient $$m=\frac{2+1}{-4-4}=-\frac{3}{8}.$$ Equation: $$y+1=-\frac{3}{8}(x-4)\Rightarrow3x+8y-4=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Lines $$y=-2x+1$$ and $$y=x+7$$ intersect at $$L$$. Point $$M(-3,1).$$ Find equation of line joining $$L$$ and $$M$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find $$L$$ by solving equations, then use gradient formula.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The line $$y=2x-10$$ meets the x-axis at $$A$$, and $$y=-2x+4$$ meets the y-axis at $$B$$. Find the equation of the line joining $$A$$ and $$B$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find $$A$$ using $$y=0$$ and $$B$$ using $$x=0$$, then apply the gradient formula.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: At $$y=0$$: $$2x-10=0\Rightarrow x=5\Rightarrow A(5,0).$$ At $$x=0$$: $$y=4\Rightarrow B(0,4).$$ Gradient $$m=\frac{4-0}{0-5}=-\frac45.$$ Using point-slope form: $$y-0=-\frac45(x-5)\Rightarrow4x+5y-20=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The line $$y=4x+5$$ meets the y-axis at $$C$$, and $$y=-3x-15$$ meets the x-axis at $$D$$. Find the equation of line joining $$C$$ and $$D$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find intercepts first, then compute gradient.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: $$C(0,5).$$ For $$y=0$$: $$-3x-15=0\Rightarrow x=-5\Rightarrow D(-5,0).$$ Gradient $$m=\frac{0-5}{-5-0}=1.$$ Equation $$y-5=1(x-0)\Rightarrow x-y+5=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The lines $$y=x-5$$ and $$y=3x-13$$ intersect at $$S$$. Point $$T(-4,2)$$ is given. Find the equation of the line through $$S$$ and $$T$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find intersection point $$S$$ first, then use two-point form.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: At intersection: $$x-5=3x-13\Rightarrow2x=8\Rightarrow x=4,y=-1\Rightarrow S(4,-1).$$ Gradient $$m=\frac{2+1}{-4-4}=-\frac38.$$ Equation: $$y+1=-\frac38(x-4)\Rightarrow3x+8y-4=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Solve simultaneous equations to find $$L$$.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The lines $$3x-y=7$$ and $$x+2y=11$$ intersect at $$G$$. Point $$H(-2,1)$$ is given. Find equation of $$GH$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Solve simultaneous equations for $$G$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: From first $$y=3x-7.$$ Substitute: $$x+2(3x-7)=11\Rightarrow7x=25\Rightarrow x=\frac{25}{7},y=\frac{26}{7}.$$ Gradient $$m=\frac{1-\frac{26}{7}}{-2-\frac{25}{7}}=\frac{19}{39}.$$ Equation found using two-point form.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The line $$y=7-3x$$ meets the x-axis at $$J$$ and $$y=2x+1$$ meets the y-axis at $$K$$. Find equation of $$JK$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find intercepts then gradient.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The lines $$y=2x+3$$ and $$4x+y=1$$ intersect at $$L$$. Point $$M(1,-4)$$ is given. Find equation of $$LM$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Solve for intersection first.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: From second $$y=1-4x.$$ Substitute: $$2x+3=1-4x\Rightarrow6x=-2\Rightarrow x=-\frac13,y=\frac73.$$ Gradient $$m=\frac{-4-\frac73}{1+\frac13}=-\frac{19}{4}.$$ Equation obtained using point-slope form.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The line $$y=2x+8$$ meets the y-axis at $$M$$, and the line $$y=-4x+4$$ meets the x-axis at $$N$$. Find the equation of the line joining $$M$$ and $$N$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find $$M$$ by setting $$x=0$$ and $$N$$ by setting $$y=0$$, then use two-point form.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: At $$x=0,$$ $$y=8\Rightarrow M(0,8).$$ At $$y=0,$$ $$-4x+4=0\Rightarrow x=1\Rightarrow N(1,0).$$ Gradient $$m=\frac{0-8}{1-0}=-8.$$ Equation $$y-8=-8(x-0)\Rightarrow8x+y-8=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The lines $$y=5x-7$$ and $$y=-x+9$$ intersect at $$P$$. Point $$Q(2,-4)$$ is given. Find the equation of the line $$PQ$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find $$P$$ by solving the two equations, then apply the gradient formula.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: $$5x-7=-x+9\Rightarrow6x=16\Rightarrow x=\frac83,y=\frac{19}{3}.$$ Gradient $$m=\frac{-4-\frac{19}{3}}{2-\frac83}=-\frac{31}{2}.$$ Using point-slope form gives the required equation.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The line $$3y-2x=12$$ meets the y-axis at $$A$$, and $$y=4x-20$$ meets the x-axis at $$B$$. Find the equation of $$AB$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Rearrange first equation to find intercepts.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: From $$3y-2x=12,$$ at $$x=0,$$ $$y=4\Rightarrow A(0,4).$$ From $$y=4x-20,$$ at $$y=0,$$ $$x=5\Rightarrow B(5,0).$$ Gradient $$m=\frac{0-4}{5-0}=-\frac45.$$ Equation $$y-4=-\frac45(x-0)\Rightarrow4x+5y-20=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The lines $$2x+y=7$$ and $$y=3x-11$$ intersect at $$C$$. Point $$D(-1,6)$$ is given. Find equation of $$CD$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find intersection point using substitution.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: From first $$y=7-2x.$$ Substitute: $$7-2x=3x-11\Rightarrow5x=18\Rightarrow x=\frac{18}{5},y=-\frac{1}{5}.$$ Gradient $$m=\frac{6+\frac15}{-1-\frac{18}{5}}=-\frac{31}{23}.$$ Equation found using point-slope form.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The line $$y=-3x+9$$ meets the x-axis at $$E$$, and the line $$4x+y=12$$ meets the y-axis at $$F$$. Find the equation of $$EF$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find both intercepts then calculate gradient.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The lines $$y=2x+1$$ and $$y=-5x+16$$ intersect at $$G$$. Point $$H(4,-3)$$ is given. Find the equation of $$GH$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Solve simultaneously to find $$G$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: $$2x+1=-5x+16\Rightarrow7x=15\Rightarrow x=\frac{15}{7},y=\frac{37}{7}.$$ Gradient $$m=\frac{-3-\frac{37}{7}}{4-\frac{15}{7}}=-\frac{58}{13}.$$ Equation obtained via point-slope form.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The line $$5x-2y=10$$ meets the x-axis at $$J$$, and $$y=x-3$$ meets the y-axis at $$K$$. Find the equation of $$JK$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Convert first equation into intercept form.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: From $$5x-2y=10,$$ at $$y=0,$$ $$x=2\Rightarrow J(2,0).$$ From $$y=x-3,$$ at $$x=0,$$ $$y=-3\Rightarrow K(0,-3).$$ Gradient $$m=\frac{-3-0}{0-2}=\frac32.$$ Equation $$y=\frac32x-3\Rightarrow3x-2y-6=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The lines $$y=4x-1$$ and $$2x+y=11$$ intersect at $$L$$. Point $$M(6,5)$$ is given. Find equation of $$LM$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find intersection point first.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: From second $$y=11-2x.$$ Substitute: $$4x-1=11-2x\Rightarrow6x=12\Rightarrow x=2,y=7.$$ Gradient $$m=\frac{5-7}{6-2}=-\frac12.$$ Equation $$y-7=-\frac12(x-2)\Rightarrow x+2y-16=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The lines $$2y=x+4$$ and $$y=5x-8$$ intersect at $$G$$. Point $$H(-2,3)$$ is given. Find equation of $$GH$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Convert first equation to $$y=mx+c$$ form.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: From $$2y=x+4,$$ $$y=\frac12x+2.$$ Solve: $$\frac12x+2=5x-8\Rightarrow\frac92x=10\Rightarrow x=\frac{20}{9},y=\frac{29}{9}.$$ Gradient $$m=\frac{3-\frac{29}{9}}{-2-\frac{20}{9}}=-\frac{2}{19}.$$ Equation from point-slope form.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The line $$4x-3y=12$$ meets the y-axis at $$A$$, and $$y=5x-20$$ meets the x-axis at $$B$$. Find equation of $$AB$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find intercepts from each equation.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: From $$4x-3y=12,$$ $$y=-4\Rightarrow A(0,-4).$$ From $$y=5x-20,$$ $$x=4\Rightarrow B(4,0).$$ Gradient $$m=\frac{0+4}{4-0}=1.$$ Equation $$y+4=x\Rightarrow x-y-4=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The line $$y=3x+6$$ meets the y-axis at $$A$$, and the line $$y=-2x+8$$ meets the x-axis at $$B$$. Find the equation of the line joining $$A$$ and $$B$$ in the form $$ax+by+c=0$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find $$A$$ by setting $$x=0$$ and $$B$$ by setting $$y=0$$, then use two-point form and rearrange.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: At $$x=0,$$ $$y=6\Rightarrow A(0,6).$$ At $$y=0,$$ $$-2x+8=0\Rightarrow x=4\Rightarrow B(4,0).$$ Gradient $$m=\frac{0-6}{4-0}=-\frac{3}{2}.$$ Equation $$y-6=-\frac{3}{2}(x-0)\Rightarrow y=-\frac{3}{2}x+6\Rightarrow3x+2y-12=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The line $$2x-5y=10$$ meets the x-axis at $$C$$, and the line $$y=4x-12$$ meets the y-axis at $$D$$. Find the equation of the line joining $$C$$ and $$D$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find $$C$$ using $$y=0$$ in the first line and $$D$$ using $$x=0$$ in the second line, then find the line through the two points.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: For $$2x-5y=10,$$ at $$y=0$$: $$2x=10\Rightarrow x=5\Rightarrow C(5,0).$$ For $$y=4x-12,$$ at $$x=0$$: $$y=-12\Rightarrow D(0,-12).$$ Gradient $$m=\frac{-12-0}{0-5}=\frac{12}{5}.$$ Equation $$y-0=\frac{12}{5}(x-5)\Rightarrow5y=12x-60\Rightarrow12x-5y-60=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The lines $$y=2x-9$$ and $$3x+y=6$$ intersect at $$S$$. Point $$T(-3,4)$$ is given. Find the equation of the line through $$S$$ and $$T$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Solve simultaneously to find $$S$$, then use gradient between $$S$$ and $$T$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: From $$3x+y=6,$$ $$y=6-3x.$$ Set equal: $$2x-9=6-3x\Rightarrow5x=15\Rightarrow x=3,y=-3\Rightarrow S(3,-3).$$ Gradient $$m=\frac{4-(-3)}{-3-3}=-\frac{7}{6}.$$ Equation $$y+3=-\frac{7}{6}(x-3)\Rightarrow6y+18=-7x+21\Rightarrow7x+6y-3=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The lines $$y=-x+11$$ and $$2y=3x-2$$ intersect at $$L$$. Point $$M(5,1)$$ is given. Find equation of $$LM$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Convert to $$y=mx+c$$, solve for intersection $$L$$, then use two-point form with $$M$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: From $$2y=3x-2,$$ $$y=\frac{3}{2}x-1.$$ Solve: $$-x+11=\frac{3}{2}x-1\Rightarrow -2x+22=3x-2\Rightarrow5x=24\Rightarrow x=\frac{24}{5},y=\frac{31}{5}\Rightarrow L\left(\frac{24}{5},\frac{31}{5}\right).$$ Gradient $$m=\frac{1-\frac{31}{5}}{5-\frac{24}{5}}=\frac{-\frac{26}{5}}{\frac{1}{5}}=-26.$$ Equation $$y-1=-26(x-5)\Rightarrow y=-26x+131\Rightarrow26x+y-131=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The lines $$4x+y=9$$ and $$y=3x-6$$ intersect at $$P$$. Point $$Q(0,5)$$ is given. Find equation of $$PQ$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find $$P$$ first using substitution, then compute gradient to $$Q$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: From $$4x+y=9,$$ $$y=9-4x.$$ Set equal: $$9-4x=3x-6\Rightarrow7x=15\Rightarrow x=\frac{15}{7},y=\frac{3}{7}\Rightarrow P\left(\frac{15}{7},\frac{3}{7}\right).$$ Gradient $$m=\frac{5-\frac{3}{7}}{0-\frac{15}{7}}=\frac{\frac{32}{7}}{-\frac{15}{7}}=-\frac{32}{15}.$$ Equation through $$Q(0,5)$$: $$y-5=-\frac{32}{15}(x-0)\Rightarrow15y-75=-32x\Rightarrow32x+15y-75=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The line $$y=7x-14$$ meets the x-axis at $$A$$, and $$x+3y=12$$ meets the y-axis at $$B$$. Find equation of $$AB$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find $$A$$ from $$y=0$$ and $$B$$ from $$x=0$$, then use two-point form.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: At $$y=0,$$ $$7x-14=0\Rightarrow x=2\Rightarrow A(2,0).$$ At $$x=0,$$ $$3y=12\Rightarrow y=4\Rightarrow B(0,4).$$ Gradient $$m=\frac{4-0}{0-2}=-2.$$ Equation $$y-0=-2(x-2)\Rightarrow y=-2x+4\Rightarrow2x+y-4=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The line $$y=-3x+15$$ meets the x-axis at $$C$$, and $$2x+y=1$$ meets the y-axis at $$D$$. Find the equation of $$CD$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Compute intercepts, then the line through the two points.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: For $$y=-3x+15,$$ at $$y=0$$: $$-3x+15=0\Rightarrow x=5\Rightarrow C(5,0).$$ For $$2x+y=1,$$ at $$x=0$$: $$y=1\Rightarrow D(0,1).$$ Gradient $$m=\frac{1-0}{0-5}=-\frac{1}{5}.$$ Equation $$y-0=-\frac{1}{5}(x-5)\Rightarrow y=-\frac{x}{5}+1\Rightarrow x+5y-5=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The lines $$y=4x+1$$ and $$y=-2x+25$$ intersect at $$S$$. Point $$T(3,-8)$$ is given. Find equation of $$ST$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find $$S$$ by solving equations, then use two-point form with $$T$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Intersection: $$4x+1=-2x+25\Rightarrow6x=24\Rightarrow x=4,y=17\Rightarrow S(4,17).$$ Gradient $$m=\frac{-8-17}{3-4}=25.$$ Equation $$y-17=25(x-4)\Rightarrow y=25x-83\Rightarrow25x-y-83=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The lines $$y=x-9$$ and $$3x-2y=4$$ intersect at $$L$$. Point $$M(-1,2)$$ is given. Find equation of $$LM$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Rewrite $$3x-2y=4$$ as $$y=\frac{3}{2}x-2$$, solve for $$L$$, then join to $$M$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: From $$3x-2y=4,$$ $$y=\frac{3}{2}x-2.$$ Solve: $$x-9=\frac{3}{2}x-2\Rightarrow -18=-x-4\Rightarrow x=14,$$ then $$y=14-9=5\Rightarrow L(14,5).$$ Gradient $$m=\frac{2-5}{-1-14}=\frac{3}{15}=\frac{1}{5}.$$ Equation $$y-2=\frac{1}{5}(x+1)\Rightarrow5y-10=x+1\Rightarrow x-5y+11=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The lines $$y=-\frac{1}{2}x+6$$ and $$y=3x-9$$ intersect at $$P$$. Point $$Q(2,1)$$ is given. Find equation of $$PQ$$ in $$ax+by+c=0$$ form.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Solve for intersection using fractions carefully, then compute gradient to $$Q$$.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The line $$y=9-3x$$ meets the x-axis at $$A$$. The line $$y=2x-5$$ meets the y-axis at $$B$$. Find the equation of $$AB$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find intercepts then gradient.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: At $$y=0,$$ $$9-3x=0\Rightarrow x=3\Rightarrow A(3,0).$$ At $$x=0,$$ $$y=-5\Rightarrow B(0,-5).$$ Gradient $$m=\frac{-5-0}{0-3}=\frac{5}{3}.$$ Equation $$y-0=\frac{5}{3}(x-3)\Rightarrow3y=5x-15\Rightarrow5x-3y-15=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The lines $$x-y=4$$ and $$2x+3y=1$$ intersect at $$C$$. Point $$D(4,4)$$ is given. Find equation of $$CD$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Solve for $$C$$ using substitution from $$x-y=4\Rightarrow y=x-4$$.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The line $$3x+y=18$$ meets the x-axis at $$E$$. The line $$y=-2x+9$$ meets the y-axis at $$F$$. Find equation of $$EF$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find $$E$$ using $$y=0$$ and $$F$$ using $$x=0$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: At $$y=0,$$ $$3x=18\Rightarrow x=6\Rightarrow E(6,0).$$ At $$x=0,$$ $$y=9\Rightarrow F(0,9).$$ Gradient $$m=\frac{9-0}{0-6}=-\frac{3}{2}.$$ Equation $$y=-\frac32x+9\Rightarrow3x+2y-18=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The lines $$y=6x-5$$ and $$y=-x+15$$ intersect at $$G$$. Point $$H(9,0)$$ is given. Find equation of $$GH$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find $$G$$ by solving simultaneously, then join with $$H$$.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The lines $$y=2x+7$$ and $$y=\frac{1}{3}x-1$$ intersect at $$J$$. Point $$K(-6,5)$$ is given. Find equation of $$JK$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Solve intersection using fractions, then use two-point form.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Intersection: $$2x+7=\frac{1}{3}x-1\Rightarrow 2x-\frac{1}{3}x=-8\Rightarrow\frac{5}{3}x=-8\Rightarrow x=-\frac{24}{5}.$$ Then $$y=2\left(-\frac{24}{5}\right)+7=-\frac{48}{5}+\frac{35}{5}=-\frac{13}{5}\Rightarrow J\left(-\frac{24}{5},-\frac{13}{5}\right).$$ Gradient $$m=\frac{5+\frac{13}{5}}{-6+\frac{24}{5}}=\frac{\frac{38}{5}}{-\frac{6}{5}}=-\frac{19}{3}.$$ Equation through $$K(-6,5)$$: $$y-5=-\frac{19}{3}(x+6)\Rightarrow3y-15=-19x-114\Rightarrow19x+3y+99=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The line $$y=-5x+20$$ meets the x-axis at $$L$$. The line $$y=x+2$$ meets the y-axis at $$M$$. Find equation of $$LM$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find intercept points, then gradient.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: At $$y=0,$$ $$-5x+20=0\Rightarrow x=4\Rightarrow L(4,0).$$ At $$x=0,$$ $$y=2\Rightarrow M(0,2).$$ Gradient $$m=\frac{2-0}{0-4}=-\frac12.$$ Equation $$y=-\frac12x+2\Rightarrow x+2y-4=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The lines $$y=3x+1$$ and $$x-2y=10$$ intersect at $$N$$. Point $$P(7,3)$$ is given. Find equation of $$NP$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Solve for intersection using substitution from second equation.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: From $$x-2y=10,$$ $$y=\frac{x-10}{2}.$$ Set equal: $$3x+1=\frac{x-10}{2}\Rightarrow6x+2=x-10\Rightarrow5x=-12\Rightarrow x=-\frac{12}{5},y=3\left(-\frac{12}{5}\right)+1=-\frac{31}{5}.$$ Gradient $$m=\frac{3+\frac{31}{5}}{7+\frac{12}{5}}=\frac{\frac{46}{5}}{\frac{47}{5}}=\frac{46}{47}.$$ Equation through $$P(7,3)$$: $$y-3=\frac{46}{47}(x-7)\Rightarrow47y-141=46x-322\Rightarrow46x-47y-181=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The line $$2x+5y=20$$ meets the y-axis at $$Q$$. The line $$y=4-3x$$ meets the x-axis at $$R$$. Find equation of $$QR$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find $$Q$$ at $$x=0$$ and $$R$$ at $$y=0$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: At $$x=0,$$ $$5y=20\Rightarrow y=4\Rightarrow Q(0,4).$$ At $$y=0,$$ $$4-3x=0\Rightarrow x=\frac{4}{3}\Rightarrow R\left(\frac{4}{3},0\right).$$ Gradient $$m=\frac{0-4}{\frac{4}{3}-0}=-3.$$ Equation $$y-4=-3(x-0)\Rightarrow y=-3x+4\Rightarrow3x+y-4=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The lines $$3x+y=4$$ and $$y=-4x+19$$ intersect at $$U$$. Point $$V(-5,-2)$$ is given. Find equation of $$UV$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find $$U$$ by solving equations: substitute $$y=4-3x$$ into the other.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: From $$3x+y=4,$$ $$y=4-3x.$$ Substitute: $$4-3x=-4x+19\Rightarrow x=15,$$ then $$y=4-45=-41\Rightarrow U(15,-41).$$ Gradient $$m=\frac{-2+41}{-5-15}=-\frac{39}{20}.$$ Equation through $$V(-5,-2)$$: $$y+2=-\frac{39}{20}(x+5)\Rightarrow20y+40=-39x-195\Rightarrow39x+20y+235=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Line $$l_1: 3x+5y-15=0$$ meets the x-axis at $$A$$. A line $$l_2$$ passes through $$A$$ and is perpendicular to $$l_1$$. Find (a) $$A$$ (b) equation of $$l_2$$ in $$ax+by+c=0$$.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: (a) $$y=0\Rightarrow 3x-15=0\Rightarrow x=5\Rightarrow A(5,0).$$ (b) $$3x+5y-15=0\Rightarrow y=-\frac{3}{5}x+3,$$ so $$m_1=-\frac{3}{5}$$ and $$m_\perp=\frac{5}{3}.$$ Through $$A(5,0):\ y=\frac{5}{3}(x-5).$$ Multiply by $$3$$: $$3y=5x-25\Rightarrow 5x-3y-25=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Find the equation of the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining $$P(-2,7)$$ and $$Q(6,-1)$$ in $$ax+by+c=0$$ form.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Midpoint $$M=\left(\frac{-2+6}{2},\frac{7+(-1)}{2}\right)=(2,3).$$ Slope $$m_{PQ}=\frac{-1-7}{6-(-2)}=\frac{-8}{8}=-1,$$ so perpendicular slope $$m_\perp=1.$$ Through $$M(2,3):\ y-3=1(x-2)\Rightarrow y=x+1\Rightarrow x-y+1=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Find an equation of the line through $$(-3,-5)$$ perpendicular to $$7x+2y+9=0$$. Give answer in $$ax+by+c=0$$.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: $$7x+2y+9=0\Rightarrow y=-\frac{7}{2}x-\frac{9}{2},$$ so slope $$m=-\frac{7}{2}.$$ Perpendicular slope $$m_\perp=\frac{2}{7}.$$ Through $$(-3,-5):\ y+5=\frac{2}{7}(x+3).$$ Multiply by $$7$$: $$7y+35=2x+6\Rightarrow 2x-7y-29=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Quadrilateral $$ABCD$$ has $$A(-2,1),B(4,-2),C(7,4),D(1,7).$$ Show that $$ABCD$$ is a rectangle.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Show adjacent sides perpendicular and opposite sides parallel via gradients.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: $$m_{AB}=\frac{-2-1}{4-(-2)}=\frac{-3}{6}=-\frac12.$$ $$m_{BC}=\frac{4-(-2)}{7-4}=\frac{6}{3}=2.$$ Then $$m_{AB}m_{BC}=-1\Rightarrow AB\perp BC.$$ Also $$m_{CD}=\frac{7-4}{1-7}=\frac{3}{-6}=-\frac12=m_{AB}$$ so $$AB\parallel CD.$$ And $$m_{DA}=\frac{1-7}{-2-1}=\frac{-6}{-3}=2=m_{BC}$$ so $$BC\parallel AD.$$ Hence rectangle.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Quadrilateral $$PQRS$$ has $$P(1,2),Q(6,5),R(9,0),S(4,-3).$$ Show that $$PQRS$$ is a parallelogram (not necessarily a rectangle).
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Show opposite sides are parallel (equal gradients).
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: $$m_{PQ}=\frac{5-2}{6-1}=\frac{3}{5}.$$ $$m_{RS}=\frac{-3-0}{4-9}=\frac{-3}{-5}=\frac{3}{5}\Rightarrow PQ\parallel RS.$$ $$m_{QR}=\frac{0-5}{9-6}=-\frac{5}{3}.$$ $$m_{PS}=\frac{-3-2}{4-1}=-\frac{5}{3}\Rightarrow QR\parallel PS.$$ Therefore both pairs of opposite sides are parallel ⇒ parallelogram.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Quadrilateral $$ABCD$$ has $$A(0,0),B(6,2),C(4,8),D(-2,6).$$ Determine whether it is a parallelogram, rectangle, both, or neither.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Check opposite side gradients for parallelogram; check adjacent product $$=-1$$ for rectangle.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: $$m_{AB}=\frac{2-0}{6-0}=\frac13.$$ $$m_{CD}=\frac{6-8}{-2-4}=\frac{-2}{-6}=\frac13\Rightarrow AB\parallel CD.$$ $$m_{BC}=\frac{8-2}{4-6}=\frac{6}{-2}=-3.$$ $$m_{AD}=\frac{6-0}{-2-0}=\frac{6}{-2}=-3\Rightarrow BC\parallel AD.$$ So parallelogram. Also $$m_{AB}m_{BC}=\frac13\cdot(-3)=-1,$$ so adjacent sides perpendicular ⇒ rectangle. Therefore it is **both** (a rectangle).

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Lines $$l_1: y=2x+1$$ and $$l_2: x+y-7=0$$ intersect at $$P$$. Find the equation of the line through $$P$$ perpendicular to $$l_1$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find $$P$$ by solving, then use perpendicular slope to $$l_1$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Intersection: from $$x+y-7=0\Rightarrow y=7-x.$$ Set $$7-x=2x+1\Rightarrow3x=6\Rightarrow x=2,y=5,$$ so $$P(2,5).$$ Slope of $$l_1$$ is $$2,$$ so perpendicular slope $$-\frac12.$$ Through $$P$$: $$y-5=-\frac12(x-2)\Rightarrow x+2y-12=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: For what value of $$k$$ are the lines $$y=(k-1)x+3$$ and $$y=2x-k$$ perpendicular?
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use condition $$m_1m_2=-1$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Slopes: $$m_1=k-1,\ m_2=2.$$ Perpendicular condition: $$(k-1)\cdot2=-1\Rightarrow k-1=-\frac12\Rightarrow k=\frac12.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The line $$3x+ky-12=0$$ is parallel to $$2x-5y+1=0$$. Find $$k$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Parallel lines have equal slopes $$-\frac{a}{b}$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Slope of first: $$m_1=-\frac{3}{k}.$$ Slope of second: $$m_2=-\frac{2}{-5}=\frac{2}{5}.$$ Set $$-\frac{3}{k}=\frac{2}{5}\Rightarrow -15=2k\Rightarrow k=-\frac{15}{2}.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Find the perpendicular distance between the parallel lines $$4x-3y+12=0$$ and $$4x-3y-6=0$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use distance between parallel lines: $$\frac{|c_2-c_1|}{\sqrt{a^2+b^2}}$$ for $$ax+by+c=0$$.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Find the equation of the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining $$A(3,-1)$$ and $$B(9,5)$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Slope of $$AB$$ then perpendicular slope; midpoint then point-slope.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_title: Find line through point perpendicular to given
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Find the equation of the line through $$(-8,3)$$ perpendicular to $$2y-5x+10=0$$ in $$ax+by+c=0$$ form.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Rearrange to find slope; take negative reciprocal; use point-slope and clear fractions.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: $$2y-5x+10=0\Rightarrow 2y=5x-10\Rightarrow y=\frac{5}{2}x-5.$$ So perpendicular slope $$=-\frac{2}{5}.$$ Through $$(-8,3):\ y-3=-\frac{2}{5}(x+8).$$ Multiply by $$5$$: $$5y-15=-2x-16\Rightarrow2x+5y+1=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_title: Right angle check with three points
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Given $$A(1,4),B(7,1),C(3,-7).$$ Show that $$\angle ABC$$ is a right angle.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Show $$BA\perp BC$$ by slope product $$=-1$$.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Quadrilateral $$ABCD$$ has $$A(-1,2),B(5,0),C(7,6),D(1,8).$$ Show it is a rectangle by using both parallelism and a right angle.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Check $$AB\parallel CD$$ and $$BC\parallel AD$$ and verify one right angle using slope product.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: $$m_{AB}=\frac{0-2}{5-(-1)}=-\frac{2}{6}=-\frac13.$$ $$m_{CD}=\frac{8-6}{1-7}=\frac{2}{-6}=-\frac13\Rightarrow AB\parallel CD.$$ $$m_{BC}=\frac{6-0}{7-5}=3.$$ $$m_{AD}=\frac{8-2}{1-(-1)}=3\Rightarrow BC\parallel AD.$$ Also $$m_{AB}m_{BC}=-\frac13\cdot3=-1,$$ so adjacent sides perpendicular ⇒ rectangle.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_title: Find equation of altitude in triangle
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Triangle vertices $$A(1,2),B(7,5),C(3,-1).$$ Find the equation of the altitude from $$C$$ to line $$AB$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find slope of $$AB$$, then perpendicular slope; line through $$C$$ with that slope.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Triangle $$A(-4,6),B(8,2),C(2,-4).$$ Find the equation of the median from $$C$$ to $$AB$$ (line through $$C$$ and midpoint of $$AB$$).
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find midpoint of $$AB$$ then equation through two points.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Midpoint of $$AB$$: $$M=\left(\frac{-4+8}{2},\frac{6+2}{2}\right)=(2,4).$$ Median passes through $$C(2,-4)$$ and $$M(2,4)$$, so it is vertical: $$x=2.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Quadrilateral $$ABCD$$ has $$A(0,0),B(4,1),C(3,5),D(-1,4).$$ Show that it is a square.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Show it is a rectangle (parallelogram + right angle) and show adjacent sides equal using distances.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Slopes: $$m_{AB}=\frac{1-0}{4-0}=\frac14.$$ $$m_{BC}=\frac{5-1}{3-4}=\frac{4}{-1}=-4.$$ Product $$m_{AB}m_{BC}=-1,$$ so right angle. Also $$m_{CD}=\frac{4-5}{-1-3}=\frac{-1}{-4}=\frac14\Rightarrow AB\parallel CD,$$ and $$m_{AD}=\frac{4-0}{-1-0}=-4\Rightarrow BC\parallel AD,$$ so parallelogram ⇒ rectangle. Lengths: $$AB=\sqrt{(4-0)^2+(1-0)^2}=\sqrt{17},$$ $$BC=\sqrt{(3-4)^2+(5-1)^2}=\sqrt{17}.$$ Rectangle with equal adjacent sides ⇒ square.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Given $$A(1,2),B(7,4),C(5,10)$$ are three consecutive vertices of rectangle $$ABCD$$. Find $$D$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use vector/coordinate idea: for consecutive vertices, $$D=A+C-B$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: For a rectangle with consecutive $$A\to B\to C,$$ we have $$\vec{AD}=\vec{BC}$$ so $$D=A+C-B.$$ Compute: $$D=(1,2)+(5,10)-(7,4)=(-1,8).$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Points $$A(0,0),B(6,k),C(10,4)$$ form a right angle at $$B$$ (i.e., $$AB\perp BC$$). Find $$k$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use slope product condition between $$AB$$ and $$BC$$.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Find the equation of the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining $$A(6,0)$$ and $$B(0,8)$$, then find where it meets the x-axis.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Midpoint + perpendicular slope; then set $$y=0$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Midpoint $$M=(3,4).$$ Slope $$m_{AB}=\frac{8-0}{0-6}=-\frac{4}{3}.$$ Perpendicular slope $$m_\perp=\frac{3}{4}.$$ Equation: $$y-4=\frac{3}{4}(x-3)\Rightarrow4y-16=3x-9\Rightarrow3x-4y+7=0.$$ For x-axis set $$y=0$$: $$3x+7=0\Rightarrow x=-\frac{7}{3}.$$ So intersection $$\left(-\frac{7}{3},0\right).$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Points $$P(-2,1),Q(4,5),R(8,-1),S(2,-5)$$. Decide if $$PQRS$$ is a parallelogram and justify.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Compare gradients of opposite sides OR show midpoints of diagonals coincide.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Gradients: $$m_{PQ}=\frac{5-1}{4-(-2)}=\frac{4}{6}=\frac{2}{3}.$$ $$m_{RS}=\frac{-5-(-1)}{2-8}=\frac{-4}{-6}=\frac{2}{3}\Rightarrow PQ\parallel RS.$$ $$m_{QR}=\frac{-1-5}{8-4}=-\frac{6}{4}=-\frac{3}{2}.$$ $$m_{PS}=\frac{-5-1}{2-(-2)}=-\frac{6}{4}=-\frac{3}{2}\Rightarrow QR\parallel PS.$$ Hence parallelogram.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_title: Find equation of line parallel to one and perpendicular to another
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Find the equation of the line through $$(2,3)$$ that is parallel to $$3x-2y+1=0$$ and perpendicular to $$y=-\frac12x+7$$. (If impossible, explain why.)
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: A line cannot be both parallel to one line and perpendicular to another unless those two lines are perpendicular.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Check slopes: $$3x-2y+1=0\Rightarrow y=\frac{3}{2}x+\frac12,$$ slope $$=\frac{3}{2}.$$ Line $$y=-\frac12x+7$$ has slope $$=-\frac12.$$ A line perpendicular to slope $$-\frac12$$ must have slope $$2.$$ But being parallel to the first requires slope $$\frac{3}{2}.$$ Since $$2\ne\frac{3}{2},$$ no such line exists.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_title: Find equation of diagonal and show perpendicular
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Rectangle has vertices $$A(1,1),B(7,3),C(5,9),D(-1,7).$$ (a) Show it is a rectangle. (b) Show diagonals are perpendicular or not.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use slopes for right angle and parallel sides; compute slopes of diagonals.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: (a) $$m_{AB}=\frac{3-1}{7-1}=\frac{2}{6}=\frac13.$$ $$m_{BC}=\frac{9-3}{5-7}=\frac{6}{-2}=-3.$$ Product $$=-1,$$ so right angle. $$m_{CD}=\frac{7-9}{-1-5}=\frac{-2}{-6}=\frac13\Rightarrow AB\parallel CD.$$ $$m_{DA}=\frac{1-7}{1-(-1)}=\frac{-6}{2}=-3\Rightarrow BC\parallel AD.$$ Hence rectangle. (b) Diagonals: $$m_{AC}=\frac{9-1}{5-1}=2,$$ $$m_{BD}=\frac{7-3}{-1-7}=\frac{4}{-8}=-\frac12.$$ Product $$= -1,$$ so diagonals are perpendicular.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_title: Find locus line equidistant from two points
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Find the locus of points equidistant from $$A(2,6)$$ and $$B(8,0)$$. Give the equation.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Locus is the perpendicular bisector of $$AB$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Midpoint $$M=\left(\frac{2+8}{2},\frac{6+0}{2}\right)=(5,3).$$ Slope $$m_{AB}=\frac{0-6}{8-2}=-1.$$ Perpendicular slope $$=1.$$ Equation through $$M$$: $$y-3=1(x-5)\Rightarrow y=x-2\Rightarrow x-y-2=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Given $$A(-3,5),B(3,1),C(7,7).$$ (a) Find equation of line through $$A$$ perpendicular to $$BC$$. (b) Show that this line meets $$BC$$ at a right angle by calculation.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Compute slope $$BC$$ then perpendicular line through $$A$$; verify product of slopes $$=-1$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Slope $$m_{BC}=\frac{7-1}{7-3}=\frac{6}{4}=\frac{3}{2}.$$ Perpendicular slope $$m_\perp=-\frac{2}{3}.$$ Line through $$A(-3,5):\ y-5=-\frac{2}{3}(x+3).$$ Multiply by $$3$$: $$3y-15=-2x-6\Rightarrow2x+3y-9=0.$$ Verification: slope of this line is $$-\frac{2}{3}$$ and slope of $$BC$$ is $$\frac{3}{2},$$ product $$=-1,$$ so they meet at a right angle.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Find the equation of the line through $$(9,-4)$$ perpendicular to $$y=-\frac{4}{3}x+6$$. Give the answer in $$ax+by+c=0$$ form.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Negative reciprocal of $$-\frac{4}{3}$$ is $$\frac{3}{4}$$; use point–slope then rearrange.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Lines $$l_1:y=2x-1$$ and $$l_2:3x+y-11=0$$ intersect at $$P$$. Find the equation of the line through $$P$$ parallel to $$4x-2y+5=0$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find $$P$$ first; slope of required line equals slope of given parallel line.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Intersection: $$y=11-3x,$$ so $$11-3x=2x-1\Rightarrow5x=12\Rightarrow x=\frac{12}{5},y=\frac{13}{5}.$$ Slope of $$4x-2y+5=0$$ is $$m=2.$$ Line: $$y-\frac{13}{5}=2\left(x-\frac{12}{5}\right)\Rightarrow10x-5y-11=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_title: Perpendicular from a point to a line
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Find the equation of the line through $$(5,7)$$ perpendicular to $$6x+5y-20=0$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Write given line in slope form; use negative reciprocal.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Points $$A(2,1),B(8,3),C(5,-5)$$ form triangle $$ABC$$. Show the angle at $$B$$ is a right angle.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Show $$BA\perp BC$$ using slope product.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Quadrilateral $$ABCD$$ has $$A(1,3),B(5,1),C(9,5),D(5,7).$$ Show that $$ABCD$$ is a rectangle.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Show adjacent sides perpendicular and opposite sides parallel.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: $$m_{AB}=\frac{1-3}{5-1}=-\frac12,\ m_{BC}=\frac{5-1}{9-5}=1.$$ Product $$=-\frac12\ne-1,$$ check correct sides: $$m_{AB}=-\frac12,\ m_{AD}=\frac{7-3}{5-1}=1.$$ Product $$=-\frac12\ne-1,$$ but $$m_{AB}=\frac{1-3}{5-1}=-\frac12,\ m_{BC}=\frac{5-1}{9-5}=1$$ not perpendicular ⇒ **not** rectangle. However $$m_{AB}=m_{CD}=-\frac12$$ and $$m_{BC}=m_{AD}=1$$ ⇒ parallelogram only.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Find the equation of the perpendicular bisector of the line joining $$(-6,4)$$ and $$(2,10)$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Midpoint + negative reciprocal slope.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Vertices of triangle $$ABC$$ are $$A(4,2),B(10,8),C(6,-4)$$. Find the equation of the altitude from $$C$$ to $$AB$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find slope of $$AB$$, then perpendicular slope through $$C$$.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The line $$y=(k+2)x-1$$ is perpendicular to $$3x-2y+7=0$$. Find $$k$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use slope product $$=-1$$.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Points $$A(0,0),B(4,k),C(10,6),D(6,2)$$ form a rectangle. Find $$k$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use perpendicular slopes for adjacent sides.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Find the perpendicular distance between $$5x+12y-7=0$$ and $$5x+12y+23=0$$.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_title: Equation of line equidistant from two lines
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Find the equation of the line midway between $$2x-y-6=0$$ and $$2x-y+10=0$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Midway line has same $$a,b$$ and average $$c$$.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Points $$A(2,1),B(6,3),C(8,7)$$ are consecutive vertices of a rectangle. Find $$D$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use $$D=A+C-B$$.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Points $$P(1,4),Q(7,6),R(9,2),S(3,0)$$. Show $$PQRS$$ is a parallelogram using diagonals.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Show diagonals have same midpoint.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Midpoint of $$PR=\left(\frac{1+9}{2},\frac{4+2}{2}\right)=(5,3).$$ Midpoint of $$QS=\left(\frac{7+3}{2},\frac{6+0}{2}\right)=(5,3).$$ Diagonals bisect ⇒ parallelogram.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The curve $$y=x^2$$ has tangent gradient $$2x$$. Find equation of the normal at point where $$x=1$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Normal slope is negative reciprocal of tangent slope.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Tangent slope $$=2.$$ Normal slope $$=-\frac12.$$ Point $$=(1,1).$$ $$y-1=-\frac12(x-1)\Rightarrow x+2y-3=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Quadrilateral $$ABCD$$ has $$A(-2,1),B(4,3),C(6,-1),D(0,-3)$$. Show diagonals are perpendicular.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find slopes of diagonals $$AC$$ and $$BD$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: $$m_{AC}=\frac{-1-1}{6+2}=-\frac{2}{8}=-\frac14.$$ $$m_{BD}=\frac{-3-3}{0-4}=\frac{-6}{-4}=\frac32.$$ Product $$=-\frac{3}{8}\ne-1,$$ so diagonals are not perpendicular.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Find the locus of points equidistant from $$A(-1,3)$$ and $$B(5,7)$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Locus is perpendicular bisector of $$AB$$.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Given $$A(0,6),B(8,2)$$. Find equation of line through midpoint of $$AB$$ perpendicular to $$AB$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Midpoint + negative reciprocal slope.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Find the equation of the line through $$(1,-2)$$ that is perpendicular to $$y=3x+4$$ and parallel to $$6x-2y+7=0$$, or explain why impossible.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Check slope conditions for consistency.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Perpendicular to slope $$3$$ ⇒ slope $$=-\frac13.$$ Parallel to $$6x-2y+7=0\Rightarrow y=3x+\frac72$$ ⇒ slope $$=3.$$ Since $$-\frac13\ne3,$$ no such line exists.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Triangle $$A(-2,4),B(6,0),C(4,10)$$. Find equation of altitude from $$B$$ to $$AC$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find slope of $$AC$$ then perpendicular slope through $$B$$.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Points $$A(1,1),B(5,3),C(7,-1)$$. (a) Find equation of line through $$A$$ perpendicular to $$BC$$. (b) Verify perpendicularity.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find slope of $$BC$$, then negative reciprocal through $$A$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: $$m_{BC}=\frac{-1-3}{7-5}=-2.$$ Perpendicular slope $$=\frac12.$$ Through $$A(1,1):\ y-1=\frac12(x-1)\Rightarrow x-2y+1=0.$$ Verification: $$(-2)\cdot\frac12=-1,$$ so perpendicular.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use distance formula $$d=\sqrt{(x_2-x_1)^2+(y_2-y_1)^2}.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Points A(–3,5), B(–2,–2), C(3,–7). Determine whether line joining A,B is congruent to line joining B,C.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Two segments are congruent if they have equal lengths.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: P(11,–8), Q(4,–3), R(7,5). Show that segment PQ is not congruent to QR.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use distance formula for both and compare.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Distance between (–1,13) and (x,9) is √65. Find two possible x.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Substitute into distance formula and solve quadratic in x.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Distance between (2,y) and (5,3) is √10. Find two possible y.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Substitute in formula and solve for y.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: a) Show $$y=2x+4$$ is parallel to $$6x–3y–9=0$$.b) Find perpendicular line to $$l_1$$ through (3,10).c) Find intersection of $$l_1$$ and $$l_2$$.d) Find shortest distance between $$l_1$$ and $$l_2$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Shortest distance between parallel lines = perpendicular distance formula.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: a) Gradients both 2.b) Perpendicular slope = –½ ⇒ $$y–10=–½(x–3)⇒y=–½x+11.5$$. c) Substitute into $$y=2x+4$$ ⇒ x=2.5, y=9.d) Distance = |4–(–11.5)|/√(2²+1²)=15.5/√5.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: P lies on $$y=4–3x$$ and is √34 from origin. Find two possible x.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use distance formula between (0,0) and (x,4–3x).

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The vertices of a triangle are A(2,7), B(5,–6), C(8,–6). (a) Show triangle is scalene. (b) Find area of triangle ABC.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Scalene triangles have three unequal sides. We know that, Area = ½×base×height.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: a) Sides: AB=√(3²+13²)=√178, BC=3, AC=√(6²+13²)=√205 → all different. b) Area = ½×3×13=19.5.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The straight line \(l_1\) has equation \(y=7x-3\). The straight line \(l_2\) has equation \(4x+3y-41=0\). The lines intersect at the point \(A\). (a) Work out the coordinates of \(A\). (b) The straight line \(l_2\) crosses the \(x\)-axis at the point \(B\). Work out the coordinates of \(B\). (c) Work out the area of triangle \(AOB\).
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Solve \(7x-3=\frac{41-4x}{3}\) for \(A\); set \(y=0\) in \(l_2\) for \(B\); use triangle area \(\tfrac12|x_Ay_B-y_Ax_B|\).
