Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The straight line \(l_1\) has equation \(4x-5y-10=0\) and intersects the \(x\)-axis at point \(A\). The straight line \(l_2\) has equation \(4x-2y+20=0\) and intersects the \(x\)-axis at point \(B\). (a) Find \(A\). (b) Find \(B\). The lines \(l_1\) and \(l_2\) intersect at point \(C\). (c) Find \(C\). (d) Work out the area of triangle \(ABC\).
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Set \(y=0\) to get \(x\)-intercepts; solve the two-line system for \(C\); for area use shoelace or \(\tfrac12\cdot\text{base}\cdot\text{height}\).

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The vertices of a triangle are $$A(2,7),\ B(5,-6),\ C(8,-6)$$. (a) Show that the triangle is scalene. (b) Find the area of $$\triangle ABC$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use distance formula $$d=\sqrt{(x_2-x_1)^2+(y_2-y_1)^2}$$ for each side; since $$BC$$ is horizontal, use base–height for area.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: (a) $$AB=\sqrt{(5-2)^2+(-6-7)^2}=\sqrt{3^2+(-13)^2}=\sqrt{178},\quad BC=\sqrt{(8-5)^2+(-6+6)^2}=3,\quad AC=\sqrt{(8-2)^2+(-6-7)^2}=\sqrt{6^2+(-13)^2}=\sqrt{205}\ \Rightarrow\ \text{all sides different, scalene.}$$ (b) Base $$BC=3,$$ height $$=|7-(-6)|=13,$$ so $$\text{Area}=\tfrac12\cdot3\cdot13=19.5.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The straight line $$l_1$$ passes through $$(-4,14)$$ with gradient $$-\tfrac14$$. (a) Find its equation in the form $$ax+by+c=0$$. (b) Find where it crosses the y-axis (A). The line $$l_2$$ passes through the origin with gradient 3. The lines intersect at B. (c) Find coordinates of B. (d) Find the exact area of $$\triangle OAB$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use point–slope form $$y-y_1=m(x-x_1)$$ to get $$l_1$$, then set $$x=0$$ for A, solve simultaneously for B, then area formula $$\tfrac12|x_Ay_B-y_Ax_B|.$$
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: (a) $$y-14=-\tfrac14(x+4)\Rightarrow y=-\tfrac14x+13$$ → $$x+4y-52=0.$$ (b) At $$x=0,$$ $$y=13$$ → $$A(0,13).$$ (c) For $$l_2:y=3x,$$ solve $$3x=-\tfrac14x+13\Rightarrow 13=\tfrac{13x}{4}\Rightarrow x=4,\ y=12\Rightarrow B(4,12).$$ (d) $$\text{Area}=\tfrac12|0\cdot12-13\cdot4|=\tfrac12(52)=26.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A website designer charges a flat fee and a daily rate. Company A’s site takes 6 days and costs £7100; Company B’s takes 13 days and costs £9550. (a) Write an equation linking days $$d$$ and cost $$C$$ in the form $$C=ad+b$$. (b) Interpret $$a$$ and $$b$$. (c) If a third company is charged £13 400, find the number of days.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Set up two points $$(d,C)=(6,7100),(13,9550)$$ and fit $$C=ad+b$$.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The average August temperature in Exeter is $$20^\circ\text{C}$$ or $$68^\circ\text{F}$$; the average January temperature is $$9^\circ\text{C}$$ or $$48.2^\circ\text{F}$$. (a) Find a linear equation linking Fahrenheit $$F$$ and Celsius $$C$$ in the form $$F=aC+b$$. (b) Interpret $$a,b$$. (c) Convert the UK record of $$101.3^\circ\text{F}$$ to Celsius. (d) For what value is the temperature the same in both scales?
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use the two points $$(C,F)=(20,68),(9,48.2)$$ to determine $$a,b$$; then invert to convert; solve $$F=C$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: (a) $$a=\dfrac{68-48.2}{20-9}=1.8=\tfrac{9}{5},\ b=68-1.8\cdot20=32\Rightarrow F=\tfrac{9}{5}C+32.$$ (b) $$a=\tfrac{9}{5}$$ is the scale factor; $$b=32$$ is the offset (freezing point). (c) $$C=\dfrac{101.3-32}{1.8}=38.5^\circ\text{C}.$$ (d) $$C=F\Rightarrow C=1.8C+32\Rightarrow C=-40,$$ so $$-40^\circ$$ on both scales.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: In 2004 a city had 17 500 homes with internet connections. A service provider predicts an additional 750 homes will get internet each year after 2004. (a) Write a linear model for the number of homes $$n$$ with internet connections $$t$$ years after 2004. (b) State one assumption of this model.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Model linear growth from initial value.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: (a) $$n=17500+750t.$$ (b) Assumes the increase is constant at 750 homes per year (linear growth) and other factors remain unchanged.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The price–quantity model has demand $$P=-\tfrac{3}{2}Q+35$$ and supply $$P=\tfrac{5}{2}Q+1$$. (a) Draw both lines on the same axes.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Label with intercepts to guide the sketch.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Sketch notes: Demand decreases from $$(0,35)$$ to $$\big(\tfrac{70}{3},0\big)$$; Supply increases from $$(0,1)$$ with slope $$\tfrac{5}{2}$$.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Using the same model, (b) find the equilibrium values of $$P$$ and $$Q$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Set demand = supply and solve.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A ride-share company charges a fixed booking fee plus a per-km charge. Trip A is 12 km and costs £19.40; Trip B is 27 km and costs £35.15. (a) Write an equation linking distance $$d$$ (km) and cost $$C$$ (£) in the form $$C=ad+b$$. (b) Interpret $$a$$ and $$b$$. (c) If a trip costs £42.50, find $$d$$.

A print shop charges a setup fee plus a cost per poster. An order of 40 posters costs £92; an order of 85 posters costs £164. (a) Find $$C=an+b$$ where $$n$$ is number of posters. (b) Interpret $$a,b$$. (c) How many posters for £200?
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: (a) $$a=\frac{164-92}{85-40}=\frac{72}{45}=1.6,\quad b=92-1.6\cdot40=28.$$ So $$C=1.6n+28.$$ (b) $$a=£1.60$$ per poster; $$b=£28$$ setup fee. (c) $$200=1.6n+28\Rightarrow1.6n=172\Rightarrow n=107.5.$$ So maximum whole posters within £200 is $$107$$.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A phone plan charges a fixed monthly fee plus a charge per GB. In one month, 6 GB costs £23; 14 GB costs £35. (a) Model cost $$C$$ vs data $$g$$ in $$C=ag+b$$. (b) Interpret $$a,b$$. (c) Predict cost for 20 GB.

A taxi charges a flag-fall plus a per-minute charge. A 18-minute trip costs £31.60; a 35-minute trip costs £52.00. (a) Find $$C=at+b$$ where $$t$$ is minutes. (b) Interpret $$a,b$$. (c) Find $$t$$ if $$C=£60.40$$.

An electricity bill is a standing charge plus a charge per kWh. A household uses 280 kWh and pays £89.60; another uses 520 kWh and pays £149.60. (a) Find $$C=ae+b$$ where $$e$$ is kWh. (b) Interpret $$a,b$$. (c) If the bill is £200, find $$e$$.

A bureau charges a fixed fee plus a percentage per £ exchanged, modelled linearly as $$F=aP+b$$ where $$P$$ is pounds exchanged and $$F$$ is total fee. Exchanging £200 costs £7 fee; exchanging £600 costs £15 fee. (a) Find $$F=aP+b$$. (b) Interpret $$a,b$$. (c) Fee for £1000?
A tank has 120 L initially and is filled at a constant rate. After 8 minutes it has 200 L; after 20 minutes it has 320 L. (a) Find $$V=at+b$$. (b) Interpret $$a,b$$. (c) When will it reach 500 L?
A salesperson earns a base pay plus commission per sale. 12 sales give £1520; 30 sales give £2600. (a) Model pay $$P=an+b$$. (b) Interpret $$a,b$$. (c) How many sales for £3500?

A science lab records that $$0^\circ\text{C}$$ corresponds to $$273.15\text{ K}$$ and $$100^\circ\text{C}$$ corresponds to $$373.15\text{ K}$$. (a) Find $$K=aC+b$$. (b) Interpret $$a,b$$. (c) Convert $$310\text{ K}$$ to Celsius.

A chemical obeys a linear calibration $$A=ac+b$$. A solution with concentration 2.0 g/L gives absorbance 0.34; concentration 7.0 g/L gives absorbance 0.89. (a) Find $$A=ac+b$$. (b) Interpret $$a,b$$. (c) Find concentration when $$A=1.10$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use points $$(2,0.34),(7,0.89)$$ and solve.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: (a) $$a=\frac{0.89-0.34}{7-2}=\frac{0.55}{5}=0.11,\quad b=0.34-0.11\cdot2=0.12.$$ So $$A=0.11c+0.12.$$ (b) $$a$$ is sensitivity (absorbance per g/L); $$b$$ is baseline/offset. (c) $$1.10=0.11c+0.12\Rightarrow0.11c=0.98\Rightarrow c=8.909\ldots\approx8.91.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A laptop’s value decreases linearly with time. It is worth £900 when new (t=0) and £540 after 3 years. (a) Find $$V=at+b$$. (b) Interpret $$a,b$$. (c) Predict value after 5 years. (d) When will value reach £300?
A bus company charges a fixed card fee plus a fee per ride. 8 rides cost £15.60; 20 rides cost £34.80. (a) Find $$C=an+b$$. (b) Interpret $$a,b$$. (c) If you paid £50, how many rides?
A highway toll is a fixed entry fee plus a fee per mile. A 15-mile trip costs £9.50; a 55-mile trip costs £21.50. (a) Find $$C=ad+b$$. (b) Interpret $$a,b$$. (c) Distance for cost £30.50.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use two points, solve for $$a,b$$.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A town had 48 000 people in 2010. The population increases by 1 200 people each year. (a) Write a model for population $$P$$, $$t$$ years after 2010. (b) State an assumption. (c) Predict population in 2026.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Linear model from initial value and constant increase.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: (a) $$P=48000+1200t.$$ (b) Assumes constant increase of 1200 per year with no changes in migration/birth rates. (c) 2026 is $$t=16$$: $$P=48000+1200\cdot16=67200.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A heating contractor charges a call-out fee plus an hourly labour rate. 3 hours costs £170; 9 hours costs £350. (a) Find $$C=ah+b$$. (b) Interpret $$a,b$$. (c) How many hours for £470?

A fitness tracker models calories burned as $$K=at+b$$ where $$t$$ is minutes of jogging. After 20 min it shows 240 kcal; after 55 min it shows 555 kcal. (a) Find $$K=at+b$$. (b) Interpret $$a,b$$. (c) How long to burn 800 kcal?
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: (a) $$a=\frac{555-240}{55-20}=\frac{315}{35}=9,\quad b=240-9\cdot20=60.$$ So $$K=9t+60.$$ (b) 9 kcal/min; 60 kcal baseline/offset. (c) $$800=9t+60\Rightarrow9t=740\Rightarrow t=\frac{740}{9}=82.222\ldots\approx82.2\text{ min}.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A test score $$S$$ is scaled linearly to grade $$G$$ by $$G=aS+b$$. A score 50 maps to grade 62; a score 80 maps to grade 92. (a) Find $$G=aS+b$$. (b) Interpret $$a,b$$. (c) What score gives grade 100?
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: (a) $$a=\frac{92-62}{80-50}=1,\quad b=62-1\cdot50=12.$$ So $$G=S+12.$$ (b) $$a=1$$ means same step size; $$b=12$$ is added bonus. (c) $$100=S+12\Rightarrow S=88.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A utility bill is modelled as $$C=au+b$$ where $$u$$ is cubic meters used. 10 m³ costs £41; 26 m³ costs £89. (a) Find $$C=au+b$$. (b) Interpret $$a,b$$. (c) Find $$u$$ for £110.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: (a) $$a=\frac{89-41}{26-10}=\frac{48}{16}=3,\quad b=41-3\cdot10=11.$$ So $$C=3u+11.$$ (b) £3 per m³; £11 standing charge. (c) $$110=3u+11\Rightarrow3u=99\Rightarrow u=33.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A car rental firm charges a fixed insurance fee plus a daily rate. 2 days costs £98; 11 days costs £287. (a) Find $$C=ad+b$$. (b) Interpret $$a,b$$. (c) Days for £420.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: (a) $$a=\frac{287-98}{11-2}=\frac{189}{9}=21,\quad b=98-21\cdot2=56.$$ So $$C=21d+56.$$ (b) £21 per day; £56 insurance fee. (c) $$420=21d+56\Rightarrow21d=364\Rightarrow d=\frac{364}{21}=17.333\ldots$$ so about $$17.3$$ days.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A sensor outputs voltage $$V$$ linearly with pressure $$p$$: $$V=ap+b$$. At $$p=0$$ kPa, $$V=0.40$$ V; at $$p=120$$ kPa, $$V=2.20$$ V. (a) Find $$V=ap+b$$. (b) Interpret $$a,b$$. (c) Find pressure when $$V=1.85$$ V.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use points $$(0,0.40),(120,2.20)$$; then solve for $$p$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: (a) $$a=\frac{2.20-0.40}{120-0}=\frac{1.80}{120}=0.015,\quad b=0.40.$$ So $$V=0.015p+0.40.$$ (b) $$a=0.015$$ V per kPa sensitivity; $$b=0.40$$ V offset at zero pressure. (c) $$1.85=0.015p+0.40\Rightarrow0.015p=1.45\Rightarrow p=\frac{1.45}{0.015}=96.666\ldots\approx96.7\text{ kPa}.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A mixing process produces salt mass $$m$$ (g) after $$t$$ minutes as $$m=at+b$$. At $$t=4$$, $$m=38$$; at $$t=19$$, $$m=113$$. (a) Find the model. (b) Interpret. (c) Find $$t$$ when $$m=200$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use two points to find slope and intercept.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: (a) $$a=\frac{113-38}{19-4}=\frac{75}{15}=5,\quad b=38-5\cdot4=18.$$ So $$m=5t+18.$$ (b) 5 g/min increase; 18 g initial salt. (c) $$200=5t+18\Rightarrow5t=182\Rightarrow t=36.4.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A courier charges a fixed handling fee plus a charge per kg. A 3 kg parcel costs £12.50; a 9 kg parcel costs £24.50. (a) Find $$C=aw+b$$. (b) Interpret. (c) Cost for 15 kg?
A rainfall sensor output $$R$$ (mm) relates to counts $$N$$ by $$R=aN+b$$. When $$N=50,$$ $$R=12$$; when $$N=210,$$ $$R=44$$. (a) Find $$R=aN+b$$. (b) Interpret. (c) Estimate $$R$$ for $$N=300$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Two-point linear fit.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A freelancer charges a fixed project fee plus £45 per hour. If 10 hours costs £780 and 18 hours costs £1140, check whether this is consistent with the stated £45 per hour. If not, find the correct model $$C=ah+b$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Compute slope from two points and compare with 45.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Slope from data: $$a=\frac{1140-780}{18-10}=\frac{360}{8}=45,$$ consistent. Intercept $$b=780-45\cdot10=330.$$ Model $$C=45h+330.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A cyclist travels with distance model $$d=at+b$$ (km) where $$t$$ in hours. After 1 hour they have travelled 18 km; after 4 hours they have travelled 72 km. (a) Find $$d=at+b$$. (b) Interpret. (c) Find $$t$$ when $$d=120$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use two points; slope is speed.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: (a) $$a=\frac{72-18}{4-1}=18,\quad b=18-18\cdot1=0.$$ So $$d=18t.$$ (b) Speed is 18 km/h; $$b=0$$ means start at origin. (c) $$120=18t\Rightarrow t=\frac{20}{3}=6.666\ldots\approx6.67\text{ h}.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A chemical mass decreases linearly. At $$t=0$$, $$m=250$$ g. At $$t=8$$, $$m=170$$ g. (a) Find $$m=at+b$$. (b) Interpret. (c) When will $$m=0$$?
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use slope then intercept.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: (a) $$a=\frac{170-250}{8-0}=-10,\quad b=250.$$ So $$m=-10t+250.$$ (b) Mass decreases 10 g per unit time; initial mass 250 g. (c) $$0=-10t+250\Rightarrow t=25.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A scanner service charges a fixed fee plus a per-page cost. Scanning 60 pages costs £19; scanning 140 pages costs £35. (a) Find $$C=an+b$$. (b) Interpret. (c) Pages for £50?

Demand $$D$$ depends linearly on price $$p$$: $$D=ap+b$$. When price is £10, demand is 120 units; when price is £16, demand is 90 units. (a) Find $$D=ap+b$$. (b) Interpret $$a,b$$. (c) Find price when demand is 60.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: (a) $$a=\frac{90-120}{16-10}=-5,\quad b=120-(-5)\cdot10=170.$$ So $$D=-5p+170.$$ (b) Demand drops 5 units per £; 170 is theoretical demand at £0. (c) $$60=-5p+170\Rightarrow -5p=-110\Rightarrow p=22.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A car’s fuel cost is linear in miles: $$C=am+b$$. A 120-mile trip costs £18.40; a 380-mile trip costs £51.20. (a) Find $$C=am+b$$. (b) Interpret. (c) Miles for £70?
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find slope and intercept from two points.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A scale converts mass $$m$$ (kg) to reading $$R$$ by $$R=am+b$$. A 2.5 kg mass gives reading 3.1; an 8.0 kg mass gives reading 9.7. (a) Find the model. (b) Interpret. (c) Find $$m$$ when reading is 12.0.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Two-point linear fit then solve for $$m$$.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A caterer charges a fixed booking fee plus a cost per guest. For 40 guests the total cost is £1480; for 85 guests the total cost is £2650. (a) Find $$C=an+b$$ where $$n$$ is number of guests. (b) Interpret $$a,b$$. (c) Find $$n$$ if $$C=£3200$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use points $$(40,1480),(85,2650)$$; slope gives per-guest cost.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A gym charges a joining fee plus a monthly fee. Paying for 5 months costs £210; paying for 14 months costs £498. (a) Find $$C=am+b$$ where $$m$$ is months. (b) Interpret $$a,b$$. (c) Cost for 24 months?

A streaming service charges a base fee plus £0.80 per movie rented. In one month, renting 6 movies costs £12.20; renting 20 movies costs £23.40. (a) Find $$C=an+b$$. (b) Interpret. (c) How many movies if the bill is £30.60?
A locker service charges a fixed access fee plus a daily fee. A parcel stored 3 days costs £10.50; stored 11 days costs £26.50. (a) Find $$C=ad+b$$. (b) Interpret. (c) Days for £38.50?

A drone’s battery usage (in %) increases linearly with time. After 8 minutes it has used 18%; after 30 minutes it has used 62%. (a) Model usage $$U=at+b$$. (b) Interpret. (c) How long until 90% is used?
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Two-point line with $$(8,18),(30,62)$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: (a) $$a=\frac{62-18}{30-8}=\frac{44}{22}=2,\quad b=18-2\cdot8=2.$$ So $$U=2t+2.$$ (b) Usage rate 2% per minute; 2% initial overhead. (c) $$90=2t+2\Rightarrow t=44.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A bus company refunds money linearly based on days before travel. 10 days before travel refund is £72; 2 days before travel refund is £40. (a) Find $$R=ad+b$$. (b) Interpret. (c) Predict refund 15 days before travel.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: (a) $$a=\frac{72-40}{10-2}=\frac{32}{8}=4,\quad b=72-4\cdot10=32.$$ So $$R=4d+32.$$ (b) Refund increases £4 per extra day; £32 is refund at 0 days (model). (c) $$R(15)=4\cdot15+32=92.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A hot drink’s temperature decreases linearly over a short interval. At $$t=0$$ min, $$T=92^\circ\text{C}$$. At $$t=12$$ min, $$T=76^\circ\text{C}$$. (a) Find $$T=at+b$$. (b) Interpret. (c) Estimate $$T$$ at 20 min.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use two points to find slope and intercept.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: (a) $$a=\frac{76-92}{12-0}=-\frac{16}{12}=-\frac{4}{3},\quad b=92.$$ So $$T=92-\frac{4}{3}t.$$ (b) Temperature falls $$\frac{4}{3}^\circ\text{C}$$ per minute; initial temperature 92°C. (c) $$T(20)=92-\frac{4}{3}\cdot20=92-\frac{80}{3}=\frac{196}{3}\approx65.33^\circ\text{C}.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A student’s practice score increases linearly with hours of revision. After 3 hours score is 52; after 11 hours score is 76. (a) Find $$S=ah+b$$. (b) Interpret. (c) Hours needed for score 90.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: (a) $$a=\frac{76-52}{11-3}=\frac{24}{8}=3,\quad b=52-3\cdot3=43.$$ So $$S=3h+43.$$ (b) Score rises 3 marks per hour; starting level 43. (c) $$90=3h+43\Rightarrow3h=47\Rightarrow h=\frac{47}{3}\approx15.67.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A photographer charges a fixed session fee plus a fee per edited photo. 25 photos cost £245; 60 photos cost £420. (a) Find $$C=an+b$$. (b) Interpret. (c) Photos for £600?
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use two points.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A ski shop charges a fixed deposit plus £18 per day. A 4-day rental costs £110; a 9-day rental costs £200. (a) Find $$C=ad+b$$. (b) Interpret. (c) Cost for 12 days.
Energy produced $$E$$ (kWh) is modelled linearly with sunlight hours $$h$$: $$E=ah+b$$. At 3 hours, $$E=4.2$$; at 9 hours, $$E=13.8$$. (a) Find model. (b) Interpret. (c) Find $$h$$ when $$E=20.4$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Two-point fit then solve for $$h$$.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A car wash sells tokens with a fixed card cost plus cost per wash. 6 washes cost £41; 14 washes cost £73. (a) Find $$C=an+b$$. (b) Interpret. (c) How many washes for £105?
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: (a) $$a=\frac{73-41}{14-6}=\frac{32}{8}=4,\quad b=41-4\cdot6=17.$$ So $$C=4n+17.$$ (b) £4 per wash; £17 card cost. (c) $$105=4n+17\Rightarrow4n=88\Rightarrow n=22.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A library fine is a fixed admin fee plus a daily fine. Returning a book 5 days late costs £9.25; 18 days late costs £22.90. (a) Find $$F=ad+b$$. (b) Interpret. (c) Days late for £30.70.
Airport parking costs a fixed entry fee plus £9.50 per day. Parking 3 days costs £41.50 and 8 days costs £89.00. (a) Find $$C=ad+b$$. (b) Interpret. (c) Predict cost for 14 days.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Compute slope, then intercept.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A small business has linear profit $$P$$ (in £) depending on units sold $$n$$: when $$n=120$$, $$P=900$$; when $$n=200$$, $$P=1700$$. (a) Find $$P=an+b$$. (b) Interpret. (c) Units for profit £2500.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use two points then solve.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: (a) $$a=\frac{1700-900}{200-120}=\frac{800}{80}=10,\quad b=900-10\cdot120=-300.$$ So $$P=10n-300.$$ (b) Profit increases £10 per unit; break-even at $$P=0\Rightarrow n=30.$$ (c) $$2500=10n-300\Rightarrow10n=2800\Rightarrow n=280.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A savings account balance grows linearly: at month 2 the balance is £560; at month 11 it is £920. (a) Find $$B=am+b$$. (b) Interpret. (c) Find balance at month 20.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: (a) $$a=\frac{920-560}{11-2}=\frac{360}{9}=40,\quad b=560-40\cdot2=480.$$ So $$B=40m+480.$$ (b) Deposits increase balance £40 per month; initial balance £480. (c) $$B(20)=40\cdot20+480=1280.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A city collected 2 300 tonnes of recycling in 2015 and increases collection by 180 tonnes per year. (a) Write a model $$R=at+b$$ where $$t$$ years after 2015. (b) One assumption. (c) Predict collection in 2027.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Linear growth from initial.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: (a) $$R=2300+180t.$$ (b) Assumes constant annual increase of 180 tonnes. (c) 2027: $$t=12,$$ $$R=2300+180\cdot12=4460.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A café offers a card fee plus price per drink. 8 drinks cost £27.20; 20 drinks cost £56.00. (a) Find $$C=an+b$$. (b) Interpret. (c) Drinks for £80.00.

A machine produces items linearly with time. After 2 hours it has produced 180 items; after 9 hours it has produced 600 items. (a) Find $$N=at+b$$ where $$t$$ in hours. (b) Interpret. (c) Time for 900 items.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Two-point fit; slope is production rate.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: (a) $$a=\frac{600-180}{9-2}=\frac{420}{7}=60,\quad b=180-60\cdot2=60.$$ So $$N=60t+60.$$ (b) 60 items/hour; initial 60 items at $$t=0$$ (startup count). (c) $$900=60t+60\Rightarrow60t=840\Rightarrow t=14.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Energy used $$E$$ (kWh) depends linearly on heating time $$t$$ (hours): 1.5 hours uses 3.2 kWh; 4.0 hours uses 7.7 kWh. (a) Find $$E=at+b$$. (b) Interpret. (c) Find $$t$$ when $$E=10.0$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use two points; keep exact fractions if possible.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A company’s charge is linear in usage $$u$$: when $$u=150$$, cost £73; when $$u=420$$, cost £154. (a) Find $$C=au+b$$. (b) Interpret. (c) Find $$u$$ for £200.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Two-point line then solve.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A worker earns a fixed weekly allowance plus £14 per hour worked. In week A, 20 hours gives £350; in week B, 35 hours gives £560. (a) Find $$P=ah+b$$. (b) Interpret. (c) Check if hourly rate really is £14.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Compute slope from points and compare to 14.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: (a) $$a=\frac{560-350}{35-20}=\frac{210}{15}=14,\quad b=350-14\cdot20=70.$$ So $$P=14h+70.$$ (b) £14/hour; £70 allowance. (c) Since slope equals 14, it matches.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Drag force $$F$$ (N) relates linearly to speed $$v$$ (m/s): at $$v=5$$, $$F=18$$; at $$v=17$$, $$F=54$$. (a) Find $$F=av+b$$. (b) Interpret. (c) Find speed when $$F=66$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use two-point fit then solve.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A school trip costs a fixed coach hire plus a cost per student. 30 students cost £1260; 74 students cost £2316. (a) Find $$C=an+b$$. (b) Interpret. (c) Students for £3000.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Two-point fit; solve for $$n$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: (a) $$a=\frac{2316-1260}{74-30}=\frac{1056}{44}=24,\quad b=1260-24\cdot30=540.$$ So $$C=24n+540.$$ (b) £24 per student; £540 fixed coach hire. (c) $$3000=24n+540\Rightarrow24n=2460\Rightarrow n=102.5$$ so about $$102$$ students.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Sea level (mm) relative to a baseline rises linearly. In 2000 it was 0 mm; in 2018 it was 54 mm. (a) Model $$S=at+b$$ where $$t$$ years after 2000. (b) Interpret. (c) Predict level in 2030.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: (a) $$a=\frac{54}{18}=3,\quad b=0.$$ So $$S=3t.$$ (b) 3 mm per year rise; 0 at year 2000 baseline. (c) 2030: $$t=30,$$ $$S=90\text{ mm}.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A map uses linear conversion between miles $$m$$ and kilometers $$k$$. You know 10 miles is 16.1 km and 50 miles is 80.5 km. (a) Find $$k=am+b$$. (b) Interpret. (c) Convert 73 miles.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Two points; should give zero intercept.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A sensor reading $$R$$ is corrected to true value $$T$$ by $$T=aR+b$$. When $$R=12.0$$, true value is 11.6; when $$R=48.0$$, true value is 46.4. (a) Find $$T=aR+b$$. (b) Interpret. (c) Correct a reading of 60.0.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Two-point fit.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: (a) $$a=\frac{46.4-11.6}{48-12}=\frac{34.8}{36}=0.966\overline{6},\quad b=11.6-a\cdot12=0.0.$$ So $$T=\frac{29}{30}R.$$ (b) Scale factor $\frac{29}{30}$ reduces readings; no offset. (c) $$T=\frac{29}{30}\cdot60=58.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Battery percentage remaining $$P$$ decreases linearly with time $$t$$ (hours). At $$t=1$$, $$P=92$$; at $$t=6$$, $$P=67$$. (a) Find $$P=at+b$$. (b) Interpret. (c) When will $$P=20$$?
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Two-point fit then solve for time.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: (a) $$a=\frac{67-92}{6-1}=-5,\quad b=92-(-5)\cdot1=97.$$ So $$P=-5t+97.$$ (b) Battery drops 5% per hour; initial would be 97% at $t=0$ (model). (c) $$20=-5t+97\Rightarrow5t=77\Rightarrow t=15.4.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A concert charges a fixed online booking fee plus price per ticket. Buying 2 tickets costs £78; buying 7 tickets costs £203. (a) Find $$C=an+b$$. (b) Interpret. (c) Tickets for £328.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: (a) $$a=\frac{203-78}{7-2}=\frac{125}{5}=25,\quad b=78-25\cdot2=28.$$ So $$C=25n+28.$$ (b) £25 per ticket; £28 booking fee. (c) $$328=25n+28\Rightarrow25n=300\Rightarrow n=12.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A paint mix costs a fixed lab fee plus cost proportional to liters. 3.5 L costs £52.00; 9.0 L costs £134.50. (a) Find $$C=aL+b$$. (b) Interpret. (c) Liters for £200?
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Two-point fit; keep decimals carefully.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_title: Line through P and given gradient
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The straight line through $$P(2,1)$$ and $$Q(k,11)$$ has gradient $$-\tfrac{5}{12}$$. (a) Find the equation of the line (in $$x,y$$ only). (b) Determine the value of $$k$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use point–slope through \(P\).

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Points \(A(k,1)\) and \(B(8,2k-1)\) have gradient $$\tfrac{1}{3}$$. (a) Show that $$k=2$$. (b) Find an equation of the line through \(A\) and \(B\).
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Set gradient formula equal to \(1/3\).

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The line $$L_1$$ has gradient $$\tfrac{1}{2}$$ and passes through $$A(2,2)$$. The line $$L_2$$ has gradient $$-1$$ and passes through the point $$B(4,8)$$. The lines $$L_1$$ and $$L_2$$ intersect at the point $$C$$. (a) Find an equation for $$L_1$$ and an equation for $$L_2$$. (b) Determine the coordinates of $$C$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use point–slope form for each and solve simultaneously.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Find an equation of the line $$l$$ which passes through the points $$A(1,0)$$ and $$B(5,6)$$. The line $$m$$ with equation $$2x+3y=15$$ meets $$l$$ at the point $$C$$. (a) Find the equation of $$l$$. (b) Determine the coordinates of $$C$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find gradient of $$AB$$, then use point–slope and substitution.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The line $$L$$ passes through the points $$A(1,3)$$ and $$B(-19,-19)$$. Find an equation of $$L$$ in the form $$ax+by+c=0$$, where $$a,b,c$$ are integers.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find gradient and use point–slope, then rearrange.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The straight line $$l_1$$ passes through the points $$A(2,2)$$ and $$B(6,0)$$. (a) Find an equation of $$l_1$$. The straight line $$l_2$$ passes through the point $$C(-9,0)$$ and has gradient $$\tfrac{1}{4}$$. (b) Find an equation of $$l_2$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use gradient and point–slope for both lines.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The straight line $$L$$ passes through $$A(1,3\sqrt{3})$$ and $$B(2+\sqrt{3},3+4\sqrt{3})$$. Show that $$L$$ meets the $$x$$-axis at the point $$(-2,0)$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find gradient and verify intersection by setting $$y=0$$.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The points $$A(-4,6)$$ and $$B(2,8)$$ are joined by a line $$AB$$. A line $$p$$ is drawn perpendicular to $$AB$$ and meets the $$y$$-axis at the point $$C$$. (a) Find an equation of the line $$p$$. (b) Determine the coordinates of $$C$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find slope of $$AB$$, then use negative reciprocal and y-intercept.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: (a) $$m_{AB}=\tfrac{8-6}{2-(-4)}=\tfrac{1}{3}\Rightarrow m_p=-3;$$ $$y=-3x+c.$$ Using midpoint $$M(-1,7):7=-3(-1)+c\Rightarrow c=4\Rightarrow y=-3x+4.$$ (b) $$x=0\Rightarrow C(0,4).$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The line $$l$$ has equation $$2x-y-1=0.$$ The line $$m$$ passes through the point $$A(0,4)$$ and is perpendicular to line $$l.$$ (a) Find an equation of $$m.$$ (b) Show that the lines $$l$$ and $$m$$ intersect at the point $$P(2,3).$$ The line $$n$$ passes through the point $$B(3,0)$$ and is parallel to the line $$m.$$ (c) Find the coordinates of the point of intersection of the lines $$l$$ and $$n.$$
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use gradient relationships: perpendicular lines satisfy $$m_1m_2=-1$$, parallel lines share the same gradient.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: (a) For $$l:2x-y-1=0\Rightarrow y=2x-1\Rightarrow m_1=2.$$ ⟹ $$m_2=-\tfrac{1}{2}.$$ Equation of $$m: y-4=-\tfrac{1}{2}(x-0)\Rightarrow y=-\tfrac{1}{2}x+4.$$ (b) Substitute $$x=2$$ into $$y=-\tfrac{1}{2}x+4\Rightarrow y=3,$$ giving $$P(2,3).$$ (c) For $$n$$ parallel to $$m: y-0=-\tfrac{1}{2}(x-3)\Rightarrow y=-\tfrac{1}{2}x+\tfrac{3}{2}.$$ Intersection with $$l:y=2x-1\Rightarrow2x-1=-\tfrac{1}{2}x+\tfrac{3}{2}\Rightarrow\tfrac{5}{2}x=\tfrac{5}{2}\Rightarrow x=1,\ y=1.$$ Thus $$C(1,1).$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The line $$l$$ passes through the points $$A(0,-2)$$ and $$B(6,7).$$ The line $$n$$ has equation $$x+y=8$$ and cuts the $$y$$-axis at point $$C.$$ The lines $$l$$ and $$n$$ intersect at $$D.$$ (a) Find an equation of $$l.$$ (b) Find the coordinates of $$C.$$ (c) Find the coordinates of $$D.$$ (d) Find the area of triangle $$ACD.$$
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find gradient and use two-point form for $$l,$$ intersection by substitution, area by coordinate formula.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: (a) $$m=\tfrac{7-(-2)}{6-0}=\tfrac{9}{6}=\tfrac{3}{2};\ y+2=\tfrac{3}{2}x\Rightarrow3x-2y-4=0.$$ (b) For $$x=0,$$ $$y=8\Rightarrow C(0,8).$$ (c) Solve $$3x-2y-4=0$$ and $$x+y=8$$: substitute $$y=8-x\Rightarrow3x-2(8-x)-4=0\Rightarrow5x=20\Rightarrow x=4,\ y=4\Rightarrow D(4,4).$$ (d) Area of $$\triangle ACD=\tfrac{1}{2}|x_1(y_2-y_3)+x_2(y_3-y_1)+x_3(y_1-y_2)|=\tfrac{1}{2}|0(8-4)+4(4-(-2))+0((-2)-8)|=12.$$ Hence area $$=12\text{ units}^2.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The points $$A(2,16)$$ and $$B(12,-4)$$ have coordinates as shown. A straight line $$l_1$$ passes through $$A$$ and $$B$$. (a) Find an equation for $$l_1$$ in the form $$ax+by=c.$$ The line $$l_2$$ passes through the point $$C(-1,1)$$ and has gradient $$\tfrac{1}{3}.$$ (b) Find an equation for $$l_2.$$
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use gradient between $$A$$ and $$B$$, apply point–slope form, and rearrange to $$ax+by=c.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The points $$A(-1,-2),\ B(7,2),\ C(k,4)$$ are the vertices of $$\triangle ABC$$, where angle $$ABC$$ is a right angle. (a) Find the gradient of $$AB$$. (b) Calculate the value of $$k$$. (c) Find an equation of the straight line passing through $$B$$ and $$C$$ in the form $$ax+by+c=0$$. (d) Calculate the area of $$\triangle ABC.$$
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use gradient formula for perpendicular lines and right-angle condition $$m_{AB}\times m_{BC}=-1.$$
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: (a) $$m_{AB}=\tfrac{2-(-2)}{7-(-1)}=\tfrac{4}{8}=\tfrac{1}{2}.$$ (b) For right angle at $$B,$$ $$m_{AB}\cdot m_{BC}=-1\Rightarrow\tfrac{1}{2}\cdot m_{BC}=-1\Rightarrow m_{BC}=-2.$$ Using $$B(7,2)$$ and $$C(k,4):4-2=-2(k-7)\Rightarrow k=8.$$ (c) $$m_{BC}=-2,\ y-2=-2(x-7)\Rightarrow2x+y-16=0.$$ (d) Base $$AB=8\sqrt{1^2+(0.5)^2}=\sqrt{80}=8.94,$$ height $$=|4-2|=2,$$ so $$\text{Area}=\tfrac{1}{2}\cdot8\cdot4=16.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Find an equation of the straight line passing through the points with coordinates $$(-1,5)$$ and $$(4,-2)$$, giving your answer in the form $$ax+by+c=0$$, where $$a,b,c$$ are integers. The line crosses the x-axis at point $$A$$ and the y-axis at point $$B$$, and $$O$$ is the origin. (a) Find an equation of the line. (b) Find the area of $$\triangle AOB.$$
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find gradient and use two-point form, then use intercepts to calculate area with coordinate formula.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The straight line $$l_1$$ has equation $$4y+x=0.$$ The straight line $$l_2$$ has equation $$y=2x-3.$$ (a) On the same axes, sketch both lines showing coordinates of intercepts. (b) The lines $$l_1$$ and $$l_2$$ intersect at point $$A$$. Calculate exact fractions for $$A$$. (c) Find an equation of the line through $$A$$ which is perpendicular to $$l_1$$, in the form $$ax+by+c=0.$$
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use intercepts, substitution, and perpendicular slope relation $$m_1m_2=-1.$$
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: (a) For $$l_1:4y+x=0\Rightarrow y=-\tfrac{1}{4}x$$ (passes through $$(0,0)$$ and $$(4,-1)$$). For $$l_2:y=2x-3$$ (intercepts $$(0,-3)$$ and $$(\tfrac{3}{2},0)$$). (b) Intersection: $$-\tfrac{1}{4}x=2x-3\Rightarrow9x=12\Rightarrow x=\tfrac{4}{3},y=-\tfrac{1}{3}\Rightarrow A(\tfrac{4}{3},-\tfrac{1}{3}).$$ (c) $$m_{l_1}=-\tfrac{1}{4}\Rightarrow m_\perp=4.$$ Equation through $$A: y+\tfrac{1}{3}=4(x-\tfrac{4}{3})\Rightarrow4x-y-\tfrac{17}{3}=0\Rightarrow12x-3y-17=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The points $$A(4,6)$$ and $$B(12,2)$$ are given. The straight line $$l_1$$ passes through $$A$$ and $$B.$$ (a) Find the equation of $$l_1$$ in the form $$ax+by+c=0.$$ The straight line $$l_2$$ passes through the origin and has gradient $$-\tfrac{2}{3}.$$ (b) Write down an equation for $$l_2.$$ The lines $$l_1$$ and $$l_2$$ intersect at point $$C.$$ (c) Find the coordinates of $$C.$$ (d) Show that lines $$OA$$ and $$OC$$ are perpendicular, where $$O$$ is the origin. (e) Work out the lengths of $$OA$$ and $$OC$$ in the form $$k\sqrt{13}.$$ (f) Hence calculate the area of $$\triangle OAC.$$
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use two-point form for $$l_1$$, solve for intersection, then apply perpendicularity and distance formula.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: (a) $$m=\tfrac{2-6}{12-4}=-\tfrac{1}{2},\ y-6=-\tfrac{1}{2}(x-4)\Rightarrow x+2y-16=0.$$ (b) $$y=-\tfrac{2}{3}x.$$ (c) Solve $$x+2(-\tfrac{2}{3}x)-16=0\Rightarrow -\tfrac{1}{3}x=16\Rightarrow x=-48,\ y=32\Rightarrow C(-48,32).$$ (d) $$m_{OA}=\tfrac{6-0}{4-0}=\tfrac{3}{2},\ m_{OC}=\tfrac{32-0}{-48-0}=-\tfrac{2}{3},\ m_{OA}m_{OC}=-1\Rightarrow\text{perpendicular.}$$ (e) $$OA=\sqrt{4^2+6^2}=\sqrt{52}=2\sqrt{13},\ OC=\sqrt{(-48)^2+32^2}=\sqrt{64\times52}=8\sqrt{13}.$$ (f) $$\text{Area}=\tfrac{1}{2}(OA\times OC)=\tfrac{1}{2}(2\sqrt{13}\times8\sqrt{13})=104.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Point $$A$$ is $$(-1,5).$$ Let $$(x,y)$$ be any point on the line $$y=3x.$$ (a) Write an equation in terms of $$x$$ for the distance between $$(x,y)$$ and $$A(-1,5).$$ (b) Find coordinates of the two points $$B$$ and $$C$$ on the line $$y=3x$$ that are a distance of $$\sqrt{74}$$ from $$(-1,5).$$ (c) Find the equation of the line $$l_1$$ perpendicular to $$y=3x$$ and passing through $$(-1,5).$$ (d) Find the coordinates of the intersection of $$l_1$$ and $$y=3x.$$ (e) Find the area of $$\triangle ABC.$$
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use distance formula, substitution, perpendicular slope relation, and area formula.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Find the area of the triangle with vertices $$A(-2,-2),\ B(13,8),\ C(-4,14).$$
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use coordinate area formula $$\text{Area}=\tfrac12|x_1(y_2-y_3)+x_2(y_3-y_1)+x_3(y_1-y_2)|.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The straight lines $$l_1:y=2x-3$$ and $$l_2:3x+y-11=0$$ intersect at point $$A$$. (a) Find the coordinates of $$A$$. (b) Find the exact distance from $$A$$ to the origin $$O$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Solve simultaneously to get $$A$$; then use $$OA=\sqrt{x_A^2+y_A^2}$$ and simplify.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: (a) From $$l_2:3x+y-11=0\Rightarrow y=11-3x.$$ Substitute into $$l_1:$$ $$11-3x=2x-3\Rightarrow 14=5x\Rightarrow x=\frac{14}{5}.$$ Then $$y=2\cdot\frac{14}{5}-3=\frac{28}{5}-\frac{15}{5}=\frac{13}{5}.$$ So $$A\!\left(\frac{14}{5},\frac{13}{5}\right).$$ (b) $$OA=\sqrt{\left(\frac{14}{5}\right)^2+\left(\frac{13}{5}\right)^2}=\sqrt{\frac{196+169}{25}}=\frac{\sqrt{365}}{5}.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The line $$y=-\frac12x+6$$ cuts the $$y$$-axis at $$A$$ and the $$x$$-axis at $$B$$. (a) Find $$A$$ and $$B$$. (b) Find the area of triangle $$OAB$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Set $$x=0$$ for $$A$$; set $$y=0$$ for $$B$$; use $$\text{Area}=\frac12\cdot OA\cdot OB$$ because it is right-angled at $$O$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: (a) For $$A,$$ set $$x=0: y=6\Rightarrow A(0,6).$$ For $$B,$$ set $$y=0: 0=-\frac12x+6\Rightarrow \frac12x=6\Rightarrow x=12\Rightarrow B(12,0).$$ (b) Since $$OA=6$$ and $$OB=12,$$ $$\text{Area}=\frac12\cdot 6\cdot 12=36.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The line $$l$$ has equation $$y=3x-4$$. Find the acute angle $$\theta$$ that $$l$$ makes with the positive $$x$$-axis, correct to $$1$$ decimal place.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: For a line $$y=mx+c,$$ $$\tan\theta=m$$. Take inverse tangent and round.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Here $$m=3,$$ so $$\tan\theta=3\Rightarrow \theta=\tan^{-1}(3).$$ Using a calculator, $$\theta\approx71.565^\circ,$$ so $$\theta\approx71.6^\circ$$ (to 1 d.p.).

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Find the perpendicular distance from the point $$P(4,-1)$$ to the line $$3x-4y+5=0$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use distance formula from point to line: $$d=\frac{|ax_0+by_0+c|}{\sqrt{a^2+b^2}}$$.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Points $$A(2,3)$$ and $$B(10,-1)$$ are joined. (a) Find the midpoint $$M$$ of $$AB$$. (b) Find the equation of the line through $$M$$ parallel to $$y=4x-7$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use midpoint formula; parallel lines have same gradient; use point–slope form.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: (a) $$M=\left(\frac{2+10}{2},\frac{3+(-1)}{2}\right)=(6,1).$$ (b) A line parallel to $$y=4x-7$$ has gradient $$4.$$ Through $$M(6,1):$$ $$y-1=4(x-6)\Rightarrow y-1=4x-24\Rightarrow y=4x-23.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The lines $$y=5x-9$$ and $$y=ax+3$$ intersect at $$(2,1)$$. Find the value of $$a$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Substitute the intersection point into the second line to form an equation for $$a$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Check the point fits the first line: $$1=5(2)-9=1$$ (correct). For the second line, substitute $$(2,1):$$ $$1=2a+3\Rightarrow 2a=-2\Rightarrow a=-1.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The line $$y=mx+4$$ is parallel to $$3x-2y+7=0$$. Find $$m$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Rewrite the general form as $$y=mx+c$$, then match gradients.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: $$3x-2y+7=0\Rightarrow -2y=-3x-7\Rightarrow y=\frac{3}{2}x+\frac{7}{2}.$$ The gradient is $$\frac{3}{2}$$, so for parallelism $$m=\frac{3}{2}.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The vertices of a triangle are $$A(1,2),B(5,4),C(7,0)$$. Show that $$\angle ABC$$ is a right angle.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Compute gradients of $$AB$$ and $$BC$$ and show their product is $$-1$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Gradient $$m_{AB}=\frac{4-2}{5-1}=\frac{2}{4}=\frac12.$$ Gradient $$m_{BC}=\frac{0-4}{7-5}=\frac{-4}{2}=-2.$$ Since $$m_{AB}\cdot m_{BC}=\frac12\cdot(-2)=-1,$$ the lines $$AB$$ and $$BC$$ are perpendicular, so $$\angle ABC=90^\circ.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A line passes through $$(3,-2)$$ and makes an angle of $$45^\circ$$ with the positive $$x$$-axis. Find its equation.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Convert angle to slope via $$m=\tan\theta$$, then use point–slope form.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Find the distance between the parallel lines $$4x-3y+1=0$$ and $$4x-3y-11=0$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use $$d=\frac{|c_2-c_1|}{\sqrt{a^2+b^2}}$$ for $$ax+by+c=0$$.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The point $$P(x,y)$$ is equidistant from $$A(2,0)$$ and $$B(8,4)$$. Find the equation of the locus of $$P$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: The locus is the perpendicular bisector of segment $$AB$$: use midpoint and perpendicular slope.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Midpoint $$M=\left(\frac{2+8}{2},\frac{0+4}{2}\right)=(5,2).$$ Gradient $$m_{AB}=\frac{4-0}{8-2}=\frac{4}{6}=\frac23.$$ Perpendicular gradient $$m_\perp=-\frac32.$$ Equation through $$M(5,2):$$ $$y-2=-\frac32(x-5).$$ Multiply by $$2:$$ $$2y-4=-3x+15\Rightarrow 3x+2y-19=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The lines $$y=x+1$$ and $$y=-2x+7$$ intersect at $$A$$. Together with the $$y$$-axis they form a triangle. Find its area.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find y-intercepts on the y-axis, and the intersection point; then use base–height.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Y-intercepts: for $$y=x+1,$$ at $$x=0$$ gives $$P(0,1).$$ For $$y=-2x+7,$$ at $$x=0$$ gives $$Q(0,7).$$ Intersection: $$x+1=-2x+7\Rightarrow3x=6\Rightarrow x=2,$$ then $$y=3,$$ so $$A(2,3).$$ Base $$PQ=7-1=6$$ (on y-axis). The perpendicular height from $$A$$ to y-axis is its x-coordinate $$=2.$$ Area $$=\frac12\cdot6\cdot2=6.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The line $$y=2x+c$$ passes through the intersection of $$x=3y$$ and $$x+y=8$$. Find $$c$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Solve the system for the intersection point, then substitute into $$y=2x+c$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: From $$x=3y$$ and $$x+y=8:$$ substitute $$3y+y=8\Rightarrow4y=8\Rightarrow y=2.$$ Then $$x=3y=6.$$ Substitute into $$y=2x+c:$$ $$2=2(6)+c\Rightarrow 2=12+c\Rightarrow c=-10.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Triangle vertices are $$A(1,3),B(7,5),C(5,-1).$$ Find the equation of the median from $$C$$ to $$AB$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Median goes through $$C$$ and midpoint of $$AB$$. Find midpoint, then use two-point form.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Midpoint of $$AB$$: $$M=\left(\frac{1+7}{2},\frac{3+5}{2}\right)=(4,4).$$ Line through $$C(5,-1)$$ and $$M(4,4)$$ has slope $$m=\frac{4-(-1)}{4-5}=\frac{5}{-1}=-5.$$ So $$y+1=-5(x-5)\Rightarrow y+1=-5x+25\Rightarrow y=-5x+24.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The region $$R$$ satisfies $$y\le2x-1$$ and $$y\ge -x+4$$. (a) Find the intersection point of the boundary lines. (b) Describe the solution region.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Solve the two boundary equations to find where the lines cross; region is between them.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: (a) Solve $$2x-1=-x+4\Rightarrow3x=5\Rightarrow x=\frac53.$$ Then $$y=2\cdot\frac53-1=\frac{10}{3}-\frac{3}{3}=\frac{7}{3}.$$ Intersection is $$\left(\frac53,\frac73\right).$$ (b) $$R$$ is the set of points lying **between** the two lines (above $$y=-x+4$$ and below $$y=2x-1$$), including both boundary lines.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Show that the points $$A(-1,2),B(3,4),C(7,6)$$ are collinear.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Compute gradients between pairs; if equal, points lie on same line.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: $$m_{AB}=\frac{4-2}{3-(-1)}=\frac{2}{4}=\frac12.$$ $$m_{BC}=\frac{6-4}{7-3}=\frac{2}{4}=\frac12.$$ Since $$m_{AB}=m_{BC},$$ the points are collinear. (Equivalently, the line through $$A,B$$ is $$y-2=\frac12(x+1)\Rightarrow y=\frac12x+\frac52,$$ and $$C$$ satisfies it: $$6=\frac12\cdot7+\frac52.$$)

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The curve is $$y=x^2$$. Find the equation of the normal at the point where $$x=2$$, in $$ax+by+c=0$$ form.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find tangent slope $$\frac{dy}{dx}=2x$$ at $$x=2$$; normal slope is negative reciprocal; then point–slope.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: $$\frac{dy}{dx}=2x,$$ so at $$x=2$$ tangent slope $$m_t=4.$$ Normal slope $$m_n=-\frac14.$$ Point on curve: $$(2,4).$$ Equation: $$y-4=-\frac14(x-2).$$ Multiply by $$4:$$ $$4y-16=-(x-2)=-x+2.$$ Rearrange: $$x+4y-18=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Find the image of the point $$P(2,1)$$ after reflection in the line $$y=x$$, and state one reason why this works.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Reflection in $$y=x$$ swaps coordinates.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Reflection in $$y=x$$ swaps $$x$$ and $$y$$, so $$P(2,1)\mapsto P'(1,2).$$ Reason: points on $$y=x$$ are equidistant from $$P$$ and $$P'$$ along perpendicular directions, and the reflection exchanges horizontal/vertical components.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The line is given parametrically by $$x=1+2t,\ y=3-t$$. It intersects the line $$y=x-1$$ at $$A$$. Find $$A$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Substitute parametric expressions into $$y=x-1$$ to solve for $$t$$, then compute $$x,y$$.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The point $$P$$ divides the segment joining $$A(2,4)$$ and $$B(8,-2)$$ internally in the ratio $$1:2$$ (i.e., $$AP:PB=1:2$$). Find $$P$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use section formula: $$P=\frac{2A+1B}{1+2}$$ for ratio $$1:2$$ from $$A$$ to $$B$$.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_title: Two possible lines from distance condition
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A line through $$(-2,5)$$ intersects the y-axis at $$B$$ such that $$OB=7$$. Find the possible equations of the line.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Points on y-axis with distance 7 from origin are $$B(0,7)$$ or $$B(0,-7)$$. Find line through each pair of points.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: If $$B(0,7):$$ slope $$m=\frac{7-5}{0-(-2)}=\frac{2}{2}=1.$$ Equation $$y-5=1(x+2)\Rightarrow y=x+7.$$ If $$B(0,-7):$$ slope $$m=\frac{-7-5}{0-(-2)}=\frac{-12}{2}=-6.$$ Equation $$y-5=-6(x+2)\Rightarrow y=-6x-7.$$ Hence two possible lines: $$y=x+7$$ or $$y=-6x-7.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The midpoint of segment $$AB$$ is $$M(3,2)$$ and $$A(1,-2)$$. (a) Find $$B$$. (b) Find the area of $$\triangle OAB$$. (c) Hence decide whether the statement “Area of $$\triangle OAB$$ is 6” is true or false.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use midpoint formula to get $$B$$; then use triangle area formula $$\frac12|x_Ay_B-y_Ax_B|$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: (a) From midpoint: $$\left(\frac{1+x_B}{2},\frac{-2+y_B}{2}\right)=(3,2)\Rightarrow x_B=5,\ y_B=6.$$ So $$B(5,6).$$ (b) $$\text{Area}=\frac12|1\cdot6-(-2)\cdot5|=\frac12|6+10|=\frac12\cdot16=8.$$ (c) Since area is $$8\ne6,$$ the statement is **false**.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The line $$y=x-2$$ intersects the circle $$x^2+y^2=20$$ at points $$A$$ and $$B$$. Find $$A$$ and $$B$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Substitute $$y=x-2$$ into the circle equation and solve the resulting quadratic.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Substitute: $$x^2+(x-2)^2=20\Rightarrow x^2+x^2-4x+4=20\Rightarrow2x^2-4x-16=0.$$ Divide by 2: $$x^2-2x-8=0.$$ Factor: $$(x-4)(x+2)=0,$$ so $$x=4$$ or $$x=-2.$$ Then $$y=x-2$$ gives $$y=2$$ or $$y=-4.$$ Thus intersection points are $$A(4,2)$$ and $$B(-2,-4).$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The graph of $$y=2x-3$$ is translated 1 unit left and 4 units up. Find the equation of the new line.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Left by 1 means replace $$x$$ with $$x+1$$; up by 4 means replace $$y$$ with $$y-4$$ in the original equation.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Start with $$y=2x-3.$$ After translation: $$y-4=2(x+1)-3.$$ Simplify: $$y-4=2x+2-3=2x-1.$$ Hence $$y=2x+3.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The lines $$y=mx+1$$ and $$y=2x-5$$ are perpendicular. Find $$m$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: For perpendicular lines, $$m_1m_2=-1$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Slope of first is $$m$$, slope of second is $$2.$$ Condition: $$m\cdot2=-1\Rightarrow m=-\frac12.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The line $$y=kx$$ meets the line $$y=6-x$$ at point $$A$$. The triangle formed by $$A$$ and the coordinate axes has area 9. Find $$k$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find intersection coordinates in terms of $$k$$; triangle area with axes is $$\frac12xy$$ if $$A(x,y)$$ in first quadrant.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Intersection: $$kx=6-x\Rightarrow (k+1)x=6\Rightarrow x=\frac{6}{k+1}.$$ Then $$y=kx=\frac{6k}{k+1}.$$ Area with axes: $$\frac12\cdot x\cdot y=\frac12\cdot\frac{6}{k+1}\cdot\frac{6k}{k+1}=\frac{18k}{(k+1)^2}.$$ Set equal to 9: $$\frac{18k}{(k+1)^2}=9\Rightarrow \frac{2k}{(k+1)^2}=1\Rightarrow2k=(k+1)^2.$$ Expand: $$2k=k^2+2k+1\Rightarrow k^2+1=0.$$ No real $$k$$ satisfies this, so **there is no real value of $$k$$** giving area 9.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The position vector of point $$P$$ is $$\mathbf{p}=(4,6)$$. Find the equation of the line through $$P$$ parallel to $$2x-y+5=0$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Parallel lines have the same gradient. Rewrite $$2x-y+5=0$$ into slope form.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: $$2x-y+5=0\Rightarrow y=2x+5,$$ so slope is $$2.$$ Through $$P(4,6):$$ $$y-6=2(x-4)\Rightarrow y-6=2x-8\Rightarrow y=2x-2.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Minimise $$C=4x+6y$$ subject to $$x+y\le10,\ x\ge0,\ y\ge0$$. State the minimum value and where it occurs.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Feasible region is a triangle; minimum of a linear function occurs at a vertex.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Evaluate at vertices. Constraints give vertices $$A(0,0),B(10,0),C(0,10).$$ Costs: $$C(A)=0,$$ $$C(B)=4(10)+6(0)=40,$$ $$C(C)=4(0)+6(10)=60.$$ Minimum is $$0$$ at $$(0,0).$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A car’s distance from a checkpoint is modelled by $$d=80t-40$$ (km), where $$t$$ is time in hours after noon. (a) Interpret the meaning of the constant $$-40$$. (b) Find when the car reaches the checkpoint.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Interpret $$d(0)$$; solve $$d=0$$ to find time.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: (a) At $$t=0$$ (noon), $$d=-40,$$ meaning the car is 40 km **past** the checkpoint in the opposite direction of the chosen positive direction, or equivalently the checkpoint is 40 km behind the car at noon (sign depends on direction convention). (b) Checkpoint when $$d=0:$$ $$0=80t-40\Rightarrow80t=40\Rightarrow t=0.5.$$ So it reaches the checkpoint 0.5 hours after noon, i.e. 30 minutes after noon.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The lines $$y=x+2,$$ $$y=-x+6$$ and the $$x$$-axis form a triangle. Show that the triangle is isosceles.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find the three vertices (intercepts + intersection), then compare two side lengths using distance formula.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Find vertices. With x-axis $$y=0$$: for $$y=x+2,$$ $$0=x+2\Rightarrow x=-2,$$ so $$A(-2,0).$$ For $$y=-x+6,$$ $$0=-x+6\Rightarrow x=6,$$ so $$B(6,0).$$ Intersection of the two lines: $$x+2=-x+6\Rightarrow2x=4\Rightarrow x=2,$$ then $$y=4,$$ so $$C(2,4).$$ Now compare $$CA$$ and $$CB.$$ $$CA=\sqrt{(2-(-2))^2+(4-0)^2}=\sqrt{4^2+4^2}=\sqrt{32}=4\sqrt2.$$ $$CB=\sqrt{(2-6)^2+(4-0)^2}=\sqrt{(-4)^2+4^2}=\sqrt{32}=4\sqrt2.$$ Since $$CA=CB,$$ the triangle is isosceles (equal sides from $$C$$ to the base endpoints).

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Lines $$l_1: y=3x-2$$ and $$l_2: x+2y-14=0$$ meet at $$P$$. The line through the midpoint of $$OP$$ perpendicular to $$OP$$ is $$m$$. Find (a) $$P$$ (b) midpoint $$M$$ of $$OP$$ (c) equation of $$m$$ in $$ax+by+c=0$$ form.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Solve for $$P$$, then midpoint, then perpendicular slope to segment $$OP$$ and use point–slope through midpoint.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: (a) From $$l_2: y=\frac{14-x}{2}.$$ Set equal: $$3x-2=\frac{14-x}{2}\Rightarrow6x-4=14-x\Rightarrow7x=18\Rightarrow x=\frac{18}{7}.$$ Then $$y=3\cdot\frac{18}{7}-2=\frac{54}{7}-\frac{14}{7}=\frac{40}{7}.$$ So $$P\!\left(\frac{18}{7},\frac{40}{7}\right).$$ (b) Midpoint $$M=\left(\frac{0+\frac{18}{7}}{2},\frac{0+\frac{40}{7}}{2}\right)=\left(\frac{9}{7},\frac{20}{7}\right).$$ (c) Slope of $$OP$$ is $$\frac{40/7}{18/7}=\frac{20}{9}.$$ Perpendicular slope $$=-\frac{9}{20}.$$ Line through $$M$$: $$y-\frac{20}{7}=-\frac{9}{20}\left(x-\frac{9}{7}\right).$$ Multiply by $$140$$: $$140y-400=-63x+81\Rightarrow63x+140y-481=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The circle $$x^2+y^2=25$$ and the line $$y=mx+4$$ touch (are tangent). Find the value(s) of $$m$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: For tangency, perpendicular distance from origin to line equals radius 5. Write line as $$mx-y+4=0$$ and use distance formula.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Line: $$mx-y+4=0.$$ Distance from origin $$=\frac{|4|}{\sqrt{m^2+(-1)^2}}=\frac{4}{\sqrt{m^2+1}}.$$ Tangency requires $$\frac{4}{\sqrt{m^2+1}}=5.$$ Then $$4=5\sqrt{m^2+1}\Rightarrow\frac{16}{25}=m^2+1\Rightarrow m^2=-\frac{9}{25}.$$ No real solution, so **no real values of $$m$$** make the line tangent.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Lines $$l_1: 2x-y=1$$ and $$l_2: x+y=11$$ intersect at $$A$$. Find the perpendicular distance from $$A$$ to the line $$3x+4y-30=0$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Solve for $$A$$, then use point–line distance formula.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Solve system: add equations after writing $$l_1:y=2x-1.$$ Substitute into $$x+y=11:$$ $$x+2x-1=11\Rightarrow3x=12\Rightarrow x=4,$$ then $$y=7.$$ So $$A(4,7).$$ Distance to $$3x+4y-30=0$$: $$d=\frac{|3(4)+4(7)-30|}{\sqrt{3^2+4^2}}=\frac{|12+28-30|}{5}=\frac{10}{5}=2.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Show that points $$A(2,-1),B(6,3),C(10,7)$$ are collinear using triangle area.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use area formula for triangle: collinear iff area is zero.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A point $$P(5,2)$$ divides the segment joining $$A(1,-4)$$ to $$B(x,y)$$ in the ratio $$AP:PB=2:3$$. Find $$B(x,y)$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use section formula with ratio 2:3: $$P=\frac{3A+2B}{5}$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: For ratio $$2:3,$$ $$P=\left(\frac{3x_A+2x_B}{5},\frac{3y_A+2y_B}{5}\right).$$ So $$5=\frac{3(1)+2x}{5}\Rightarrow25=3+2x\Rightarrow x=11.$$ And $$2=\frac{3(-4)+2y}{5}\Rightarrow10=-12+2y\Rightarrow y=11.$$ Thus $$B(11,11).$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Points $$A(-3,1)$$ and $$B(5,7)$$. (a) Find the equation of the perpendicular bisector of $$AB$$. (b) Find where it meets the line $$y=2x+1$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find midpoint and perpendicular slope; then solve simultaneous.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: (a) Midpoint $$M(1,4).$$ Slope $$m_{AB}=\frac{7-1}{5-(-3)}=\frac{6}{8}=\frac34.$$ Perpendicular slope $$=-\frac43.$$ Equation: $$y-4=-\frac43(x-1)\Rightarrow3y-12=-4x+4\Rightarrow4x+3y-16=0.$$ (b) Solve with $$y=2x+1:$$ $$4x+3(2x+1)-16=0\Rightarrow4x+6x+3-16=0\Rightarrow10x=13\Rightarrow x=\frac{13}{10}.$$ Then $$y=2\cdot\frac{13}{10}+1=\frac{36}{10}=\frac{18}{5}.$$ Intersection $$\left(\frac{13}{10},\frac{18}{5}\right).$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Minimise $$f(x,y)=x^2+y^2$$ subject to the constraint $$x+2y=10$$. Find the minimum value and the point where it occurs.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Closest point on the line to the origin: use perpendicular from origin to the line or Lagrange multipliers.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Line slope: $$x+2y=10\Rightarrow y=-\frac12x+5.$$ Perpendicular through origin: slope $$2,$$ so $$y=2x.$$ Intersection: $$x+2(2x)=10\Rightarrow5x=10\Rightarrow x=2,$$ then $$y=4.$$ Minimum at $$(2,4)$$. Minimum value $$=2^2+4^2=20.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The line $$y=2x+1$$ intersects the parabola $$y=x^2-3x+4$$ at points $$A$$ and $$B$$. Find the coordinates of $$A,B$$ and the distance $$AB$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Equate expressions for $$y$$ to get a quadratic in $$x$$; solve; then use distance formula.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Set $$2x+1=x^2-3x+4\Rightarrow x^2-5x+3=0.$$ Roots: $$x=\frac{5\pm\sqrt{25-12}}{2}=\frac{5\pm\sqrt{13}}{2}.$$ Then $$y=2x+1\Rightarrow y=6\pm\sqrt{13}.$$ So $$A\left(\frac{5-\sqrt{13}}{2},6-\sqrt{13}\right),\ B\left(\frac{5+\sqrt{13}}{2},6+\sqrt{13}\right).$$ Distance: $$\Delta x=\sqrt{13},\ \Delta y=2\sqrt{13}.$$ Thus $$AB=\sqrt{(\sqrt{13})^2+(2\sqrt{13})^2}=\sqrt{13+52}=\sqrt{65}.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_title: Perpendicular from point to curve tangent
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The curve is $$y=x^2$$. Find the equation of the tangent at $$x=3$$ and the equation of the line through $$P(0,10)$$ perpendicular to that tangent.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find derivative for tangent slope; tangent line; perpendicular slope; line through point.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: At $$x=3,$$ point is $$(3,9)$$ and tangent slope $$m_t=2x=6.$$ Tangent: $$y-9=6(x-3)\Rightarrow y=6x-9.$$ Perpendicular slope $$m_\perp=-\frac16.$$ Through $$P(0,10):$$ $$y-10=-\frac16(x-0)\Rightarrow x+6y-60=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Reflect the point $$P(6,2)$$ in the line $$x=1$$ to get $$P'$$. Then find the equation of the line joining $$P$$ and $$P'$$ and show it is perpendicular to $$x=1$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Reflection in vertical line preserves y and mirrors x about 1: $$x' = 2\cdot1 - x$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Reflection about $$x=1$$ gives $$x'=2-6=-4,$$ and $$y'=2,$$ so $$P'(-4,2).$$ Line $$PP'$$ is horizontal since y is constant: $$y=2.$$ A horizontal line is perpendicular to vertical line $$x=1.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The lines $$y=1$$, $$y=7$$, $$y=x+1$$ and $$y=-x+9$$ bound a trapezium. Find its area.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find the four vertices by intersecting pairs, then use parallel sides lengths and height.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Intersect with $$y=1:$$ with $$y=x+1\Rightarrow x=0\Rightarrow (0,1).$$ With $$y=-x+9\Rightarrow 1=-x+9\Rightarrow x=8\Rightarrow(8,1).$$ Intersect with $$y=7:$$ with $$y=x+1\Rightarrow 7=x+1\Rightarrow x=6\Rightarrow(6,7).$$ With $$y=-x+9\Rightarrow 7=-x+9\Rightarrow x=2\Rightarrow(2,7).$$ Parallel sides are on $$y=1$$ length $$8-0=8$$ and on $$y=7$$ length $$6-2=4$$. Height $$=7-1=6.$$ Area $$=\frac12(8+4)\cdot6=36.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Points $$A(1,2),B(5,k),C(9,10)$$ are collinear. Find $$k$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Equal gradients: $$m_{AB}=m_{AC}$$.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The point $$P(a,1)$$ lies on the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining $$A(2,5)$$ and $$B(8,-1)$$. Find $$a$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Point on perpendicular bisector is equidistant from $$A$$ and $$B$$: set squared distances equal.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Quadrilateral $$ABCD$$ has $$A(2,1),B(8,3),C(10,-1),D(4,-3).$$ (a) Show that $$ABCD$$ is a parallelogram. (b) Find its area.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use gradients for parallelism; area can be found using base-length × perpendicular height or vector determinant.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: (a) $$m_{AB}=\frac{3-1}{8-2}=\frac{2}{6}=\frac13.$$ $$m_{CD}=\frac{-3-(-1)}{4-10}=\frac{-2}{-6}=\frac13\Rightarrow AB\parallel CD.$$ $$m_{BC}=\frac{-1-3}{10-8}=\frac{-4}{2}=-2.$$ $$m_{AD}=\frac{-3-1}{4-2}=\frac{-4}{2}=-2\Rightarrow BC\parallel AD.$$ Hence parallelogram. (b) Use vectors $$\vec{AB}=(6,2),\ \vec{AD}=(2,-4).$$ Area $$=|\det(\vec{AB},\vec{AD})|=|6(-4)-2(2)|=|-24-4|=28.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Find the acute angle between the lines $$y=2x+1$$ and $$y=-\frac12x+7$$. Use an exact expression and a decimal approximation.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use formula $$\tan\theta=\left|\frac{m_2-m_1}{1+m_1m_2}\right|$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Slopes: $$m_1=2,\ m_2=-\frac12.$$ Then $$1+m_1m_2=1+2\left(-\frac12\right)=0.$$ So $$\tan\theta$$ is undefined, meaning $$\theta=90^\circ.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Point $$P(1,4)$$ and $$Q(9,k)$$ satisfy that $$PQ=10$$ and the line $$PQ$$ has gradient $$\frac34$$. Find $$k$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use gradient to relate $$k$$ to x-change; use distance formula to confirm.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Gradient $$\frac{k-4}{9-1}=\frac34\Rightarrow \frac{k-4}{8}=\frac34\Rightarrow k-4=6\Rightarrow k=10.$$ Check distance: $$PQ=\sqrt{(9-1)^2+(10-4)^2}=\sqrt{64+36}=10$$ correct.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Points $$A(t,2t)$$ and $$B(4-t,6)$$ define a line $$L_t$$. (a) Find the gradient of $$L_t$$ in terms of $$t$$ (for $$t\ne2$$). (b) Find the value of $$t$$ for which $$L_t$$ is perpendicular to $$y=\frac13x+1$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Compute slope from two points; perpendicular condition with given slope.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: (a) $$m=\frac{6-2t}{(4-t)-t}=\frac{6-2t}{4-2t}=\frac{2(3-t)}{2(2-t)}=\frac{3-t}{2-t}$$ for $$t\ne2.$$ (b) Given slope $$=\frac13,$$ so perpendicular slope $$=-3.$$ Set $$\frac{3-t}{2-t}=-3\Rightarrow3-t=-3(2-t)=-6+3t\Rightarrow4t=9\Rightarrow t=\frac94.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_title: Distance between a point and intersection
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Point $$P(2,-3)$$. Lines $$l_1:y=4x-1$$ and $$l_2:2x+3y+7=0$$ intersect at $$A$$. Find the exact distance $$PA$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find intersection point, then distance to $$P$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: From $$l_2: 3y=-2x-7\Rightarrow y=-\frac23x-\frac73.$$ Set equal: $$4x-1=-\frac23x-\frac73\Rightarrow \frac{14}{3}x=\frac{-4}{3}\Rightarrow x=-\frac{2}{7}.$$ Then $$y=4\left(-\frac{2}{7}\right)-1=-\frac{8}{7}-\frac{7}{7}=-\frac{15}{7}.$$ So $$A\left(-\frac{2}{7},-\frac{15}{7}\right).$$ Distance: $$PA=\sqrt{\left(2+\frac{2}{7}\right)^2+\left(-3+\frac{15}{7}\right)^2}=\sqrt{\left(\frac{16}{7}\right)^2+\left(\frac{-6}{7}\right)^2}=\frac{1}{7}\sqrt{256+36}=\frac{\sqrt{292}}{7}=\frac{2\sqrt{73}}{7}.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_title: Equation of line from area constraint
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The line $$y=mx+c$$ cuts the axes at $$A(a,0)$$ and $$B(0,b)$$ with $$a>0,b>0$$. Given that the area of triangle $$OAB$$ is 24 and $$b=6$$, find the equation of the line.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use area $$=\frac12ab$$ to find $$a$$; use intercept form $$\frac{x}{a}+\frac{y}{b}=1$$ then convert to slope form.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Area: $$\frac12ab=24,\ b=6\Rightarrow \frac12\cdot a\cdot6=24\Rightarrow3a=24\Rightarrow a=8.$$ Intercept form: $$\frac{x}{8}+\frac{y}{6}=1.$$ Multiply by 24: $$3x+4y=24\Rightarrow y=-\frac34x+6.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Consider the line $$y=x+1$$ and the curve $$y=e^x$$. Explain (no calculator root-finding needed) why they intersect in exactly one point.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Compare monotonicity and convexity; consider function $$f(x)=e^x-(x+1)$$ and its derivative.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Let $$f(x)=e^x-(x+1).$$ Then $$f(0)=1-(0+1)=0,$$ so $$x=0$$ is an intersection. Also $$f'(x)=e^x-1,$$ so $$f'(x)<0$$ for $$x<0,$$ $$f'(0)=0,$$ and $$f'(x)>0$$ for $$x>0.$$ Hence $$f$$ decreases up to 0 and increases after 0, giving a unique minimum at $$x=0.$$ Since that minimum value is $$f(0)=0,$$ the graph touches only once ⇒ exactly one intersection point $$ (0,1).$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_title: Quadratic with line: equal roots condition
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The line $$y=kx+2$$ intersects the parabola $$y=x^2+4x+7$$. Find $$k$$ such that the intersection points have the same $$x$$-coordinate (i.e., the line is tangent to the parabola).
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Set up quadratic by equating; tangency means discriminant $$=0$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Intersection: $$kx+2=x^2+4x+7\Rightarrow x^2+(4-k)x+5=0.$$ Tangency: discriminant $$\Delta=(4-k)^2-4(1)(5)=0\Rightarrow(4-k)^2=20.$$ Hence $$4-k=\pm2\sqrt5\Rightarrow k=4\mp2\sqrt5.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Points $$A(6,2)$$ and $$B(2,10)$$. (a) Find equation of perpendicular bisector of $$AB$$. (b) Find its perpendicular distance from the origin.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find midpoint and perpendicular slope; then use point–line distance for part (b).
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Midpoint $$M(4,6).$$ Slope $$m_{AB}=\frac{10-2}{2-6}=\frac{8}{-4}=-2,$$ so perpendicular slope $$=\frac12.$$ Equation: $$y-6=\frac12(x-4)\Rightarrow2y-12=x-4\Rightarrow x-2y+8=0.$$ Distance from origin: $$d=\frac{|8|}{\sqrt{1^2+(-2)^2}}=\frac{8}{\sqrt5}=\frac{8\sqrt5}{5}.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Points $$A(1,2),B(7,4),C(5,10),D(-1,8)$$. Prove $$ABCD$$ is a rectangle using vectors.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Show opposite sides are equal and parallel and adjacent sides perpendicular via dot product.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Compute vectors: $$\vec{AB}=(6,2),\ \vec{BC}=(-2,6),\ \vec{CD}=(-6,-2),\ \vec{DA}=(2,-6).$$ Opposites: $$\vec{CD}=-\vec{AB}$$ and $$\vec{DA}=-\vec{BC}$$ ⇒ parallelogram. Dot product: $$\vec{AB}\cdot\vec{BC}=6(-2)+2(6)=-12+12=0,$$ so adjacent sides perpendicular ⇒ rectangle.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_title: Equation from perpendicular + passing through intercept
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The line $$l: 5x-2y+10=0$$ meets the x-axis at $$A$$. Find the equation of the line through $$A$$ perpendicular to $$l$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find $$A$$ by setting $$y=0$$; find slope of $$l$$ then perpendicular; use point–slope.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: At x-axis: $$y=0\Rightarrow5x+10=0\Rightarrow x=-2,$$ so $$A(-2,0).$$ Rewrite $$l: -2y=-5x-10\Rightarrow y=\frac52x+5,$$ slope $$=\frac52.$$ Perpendicular slope $$=-\frac{2}{5}.$$ Through $$A:$$ $$y-0=-\frac25(x+2)\Rightarrow5y=-2x-4\Rightarrow2x+5y+4=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The vertices of triangle are $$A(2,1),B(8,1),C(5,7).$$ (a) Find the centroid $$G$$. (b) Find equation of the median from $$C$$ and verify that $$G$$ lies on it.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Centroid is average of coordinates; median from $$C$$ goes to midpoint of $$AB$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: (a) $$G\left(\frac{2+8+5}{3},\frac{1+1+7}{3}\right)=\left(5,3\right).$$ (b) Midpoint of $$AB$$ is $$M\left(\frac{2+8}{2},\frac{1+1}{2}\right)=(5,1).$$ Median from $$C(5,7)$$ to $$M(5,1)$$ is vertical: $$x=5.$$ Since $$G(5,3)$$ has $$x=5,$$ it lies on the median.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_title: Line through intersection with given gradient
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Lines $$2x+y=9$$ and $$x-3y=-3$$ intersect at $$P$$. Find the equation of the line through $$P$$ with gradient $$-4$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Solve for $$P$$, then use point–slope with gradient -4.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Solve: from $$2x+y=9\Rightarrow y=9-2x.$$ Substitute into $$x-3(9-2x)=-3\Rightarrow x-27+6x=-3\Rightarrow7x=24\Rightarrow x=\frac{24}{7}.$$ Then $$y=9-2\cdot\frac{24}{7}=\frac{63-48}{7}=\frac{15}{7}.$$ Through $$P\left(\frac{24}{7},\frac{15}{7}\right):$$ $$y-\frac{15}{7}=-4\left(x-\frac{24}{7}\right).$$ Multiply by 7: $$7y-15=-28x+96\Rightarrow28x+7y-111=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_title: Find k for equal distances to two lines
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Find the value of $$k$$ such that point $$P(k,2)$$ is equidistant from the lines $$x-2y+3=0$$ and $$2x+y-10=0$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Set distances equal using point–line distance formula; solve for $$k$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Distance to first: $$d_1=\frac{|k-2(2)+3|}{\sqrt{1^2+(-2)^2}}=\frac{|k-1|}{\sqrt5}.$$ Distance to second: $$d_2=\frac{|2k+2-10|}{\sqrt{2^2+1^2}}=\frac{|2k-8|}{\sqrt5}.$$ Equate: $$|k-1|=|2k-8|.$$ Cases: (i) $$k-1=2k-8\Rightarrow k=7.$$ (ii) $$k-1=-(2k-8)\Rightarrow k-1=-2k+8\Rightarrow3k=9\Rightarrow k=3.$$ So $$k=3$$ or $$k=7.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Find all points of intersection between $$y=|x-2|+1$$ and $$y=-x+7$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Split modulus into cases: $$x\ge2$$ and $$x<2$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Case 1 $$x\ge2:$$ $$|x-2|=x-2,$$ so $$y=x-1.$$ Set $$x-1=-x+7\Rightarrow2x=8\Rightarrow x=4,$$ then $$y=3.$$ Valid since $$4\ge2.$ Case 2 $$x<2:$$ $$|x-2|=2-x,$$ so $$y=3-x.$$ Set $$3-x=-x+7\Rightarrow3=7,$$ impossible. Hence only intersection is $$(4,3).$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The line passes through $$A(0,b)$$ and $$B(6,0)$$ with $$b>0$$. The area of $$\triangle OAB$$ is 21. Find the line’s equation.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use triangle area $$=\frac12\cdot6\cdot b$$ to find $$b$$, then find slope and equation.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Area: $$\frac12\cdot6\cdot b=21\Rightarrow3b=21\Rightarrow b=7.$$ So intercepts are $$A(0,7),B(6,0).$$ Slope $$m=\frac{0-7}{6-0}=-\frac76.$$ Equation: $$y-7=-\frac76(x-0)\Rightarrow y=-\frac76x+7.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Points $$A(1,7)$$ and $$B(9,3)$$. Show that the point $$P(5,5)$$ lies on the perpendicular bisector of $$AB$$ by proving $$PA=PB$$, then find the equation of the perpendicular bisector.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Compute squared distances for first part; then midpoint + perpendicular slope for equation.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: First, $$PA^2=(5-1)^2+(5-7)^2=16+4=20.$$ $$PB^2=(5-9)^2+(5-3)^2=16+4=20.$$ Hence $$PA=PB,$$ so $$P$$ is on the perpendicular bisector. Midpoint $$M=\left(\frac{1+9}{2},\frac{7+3}{2}\right)=(5,5),$$ so the bisector passes through $$P$$. Slope $$m_{AB}=\frac{3-7}{9-1}=-\frac{4}{8}=-\frac12,$$ so perpendicular slope $$=2.$$ Equation through $$(5,5):$$ $$y-5=2(x-5)\Rightarrow y=2x-5\Rightarrow2x-y-5=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_title: Angle with x-axis through a point 1
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Find the equation of the line passing through $$P(3,-2)$$ and making an angle of $$30^\circ$$ with the positive $$x$$-axis. Give your answer in the form $$y=mx+c$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use $$m=\tan\theta$$, then point–slope form $$y-y_1=m(x-x_1)$$.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_title: Angle with x-axis through a point 2
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Find the equation of the line through $$(-4,5)$$ making an angle of $$120^\circ$$ with the positive $$x$$-axis. Write in $$ax+by+c=0$$ form with integers.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Compute slope $$m=\tan120^\circ$$, then use point–slope and clear denominators.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: $$m=\tan120^\circ=\tan(180^\circ-60^\circ)=-\tan60^\circ=-\sqrt3.$$ So $$y-5=-\sqrt3(x+4).$$ Rearranging: $$y=-\sqrt3x-4\sqrt3+5.$$ Multiply by $$\sqrt3$$: $$\sqrt3y=-3x-12+5\sqrt3.$$ Bring all terms: $$3x+\sqrt3y+12-5\sqrt3=0.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Find the equation of the line that makes an angle of $$45^\circ$$ with the positive $$x$$-axis and cuts the $$y$$-axis at $$-7$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use $$m=\tan45^\circ=1$$ and the intercept form $$y=mx+c$$ with $$c=-7$$.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The line makes an angle of $$60^\circ$$ with the positive $$x$$-axis and crosses the $$x$$-axis at $$x=4$$. Find its equation.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Slope $$m=\tan60^\circ=\sqrt3$$ and it passes through $$(4,0)$$.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A line passes through the origin and makes an angle of $$135^\circ$$ with the positive $$x$$-axis. Find its equation.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use $$m=\tan135^\circ=-1$$ and $$c=0$$.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_title: Angle with x-axis + two points check
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A line passes through $$A(2,1)$$ and makes an angle of $$\theta$$ with the positive $$x$$-axis such that $$\theta=\tan^{-1}(2)$$. Find its equation.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: If $$\theta=\tan^{-1}(2)$$ then $$m=\tan\theta=2$$. Use point–slope.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The line $$l_1:y=3x+1$$ and a line $$l_2$$ intersect at $$P(1,4)$$. The acute angle between $$l_1$$ and $$l_2$$ is $$45^\circ$$. Find the possible equations of $$l_2$$ in $$y=mx+c$$ form.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use angle-between-lines formula: $$\tan\phi=\left|\frac{m_2-m_1}{1+m_1m_2}\right|$$ with $$m_1=3,\phi=45^\circ$$ to solve for $$m_2$$, then use point-slope through $$P$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: With $$m_1=3$$ and $$\tan45^\circ=1:$$ $$\left|\frac{m-3}{1+3m}\right|=1.$$ Case 1: $$\frac{m-3}{1+3m}=1\Rightarrow m-3=1+3m\Rightarrow -2m=4\Rightarrow m=-2.$$ Case 2: $$\frac{m-3}{1+3m}=-1\Rightarrow m-3=-1-3m\Rightarrow4m=2\Rightarrow m=\frac12.$$ Through $$P(1,4):$$ If $$m=-2,$$ $$y-4=-2(x-1)\Rightarrow y=-2x+6.$$ If $$m=\frac12,$$ $$y-4=\frac12(x-1)\Rightarrow y=\frac12x+\frac72.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_title: Angle with x-axis + passes through intersection
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Lines $$y=x+5$$ and $$2x-y=1$$ intersect at $$P$$. Find the equation of the line through $$P$$ making an angle of $$150^\circ$$ with the positive $$x$$-axis.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: First find $$P$$ by solving simultaneously; then slope $$m=\tan150^\circ=-\tan30^\circ=-\frac{1}{\sqrt3}$$; use point–slope.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Find $$P:$$ from $$2x-y=1\Rightarrow y=2x-1.$$ Set $$2x-1=x+5\Rightarrow x=6,$$ then $$y=11.$$ So $$P(6,11).$$ Now $$m=\tan150^\circ=-\frac{1}{\sqrt3}.$$ Equation: $$y-11=-\frac{1}{\sqrt3}(x-6)\Rightarrow y=-\frac{1}{\sqrt3}x+\frac{6}{\sqrt3}+11=-\frac{1}{\sqrt3}x+2\sqrt3+11.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_title: Angle with x-axis + distance to origin
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The line makes an angle of $$30^\circ$$ with the positive $$x$$-axis and is at perpendicular distance $$6$$ from the origin. Find the two possible equations of the line.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use normal form $$x\cos\theta+y\sin\theta=p$$ with $$p=6$$; solve for $$y$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Normal form with $$\theta=30^\circ$$: $$x\cos30^\circ+y\sin30^\circ=6\Rightarrow x\frac{\sqrt3}{2}+y\frac12=6.$$ Multiply by 2: $$\sqrt3x+y=12\Rightarrow y=-\sqrt3x+12.$$ The second line at same distance on opposite side: $$x\cos30^\circ+y\sin30^\circ=-6\Rightarrow\sqrt3x+y=-12\Rightarrow y=-\sqrt3x-12.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_title: Angle with x-axis + passes through two conditions
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A line makes an angle of $$75^\circ$$ with the positive $$x$$-axis and passes through the point $$(-2,3)$$. Write its equation in the form $$y=mx+c$$, leaving $$m$$ as an exact surd.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use $$m=\tan75^\circ=\tan(45^\circ+30^\circ)=2+\sqrt3$$; then point–slope and simplify.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The line $$l$$ passes through $$A(4,-1)$$ and makes an angle of $$60^\circ$$ with the positive $$x$$-axis. Find (a) equation of $$l$$, (b) equation of the line through $$A$$ perpendicular to $$l$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: (a) Use slope $$\tan60^\circ=\sqrt3$$. (b) Perpendicular slope is negative reciprocal.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_title: Angle between line and axis + intercepts
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The line makes an angle of $$30^\circ$$ with the positive $$x$$-axis and passes through $$B(0,5)$$. Find where it meets the $$x$$-axis, and hence find the area of triangle formed with the axes.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Slope $$m=\tan30^\circ=\frac1{\sqrt3}$$; find x-intercept by setting $$y=0$$; then area $$=\frac12|x\text{-int}|\cdot|y\text{-int}|$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Equation: $$y-5=\frac{1}{\sqrt3}(x-0)\Rightarrow y=\frac{1}{\sqrt3}x+5.$$ For x-intercept set $$y=0:$$ $$0=\frac{1}{\sqrt3}x+5\Rightarrow x=-5\sqrt3.$$ Triangle with axes has intercepts $$(-5\sqrt3,0)$$ and $$(0,5).$$ Area $$=\frac12\cdot5\sqrt3\cdot5=\frac{25\sqrt3}{2}.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The line makes an angle of $$30^\circ$$ with the negative $$x$$-axis (measured anticlockwise from the negative $$x$$-axis). Find its slope and write the equation if it passes through $$P(2,3)$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Convert to standard angle from positive x-axis: $$180^\circ+30^\circ=210^\circ$$; slope $$=\tan210^\circ=\tan30^\circ=\frac1{\sqrt3}$$ but negative? check sign.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Standard angle $$=210^\circ.$$ $$\tan210^\circ=\tan(180^\circ+30^\circ)=\tan30^\circ=\frac{1}{\sqrt3}$$ (positive). Thus slope $$m=\frac1{\sqrt3}.$$ Through $$P(2,3):$$ $$y-3=\frac{1}{\sqrt3}(x-2)\Rightarrow y=\frac{1}{\sqrt3}x+3-\frac{2}{\sqrt3}.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The line makes an angle of $$135^\circ$$ with the positive $$x$$-axis and crosses the $$y$$-axis at $$9$$. Find its equation.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_title: Angle between two lines + through point
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The line $$l_1:y=-x+4$$ and line $$l_2$$ intersect at $$P(2,2)$$. If the obtuse angle between them is $$120^\circ$$, find the possible equations of $$l_2$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Use angle formula with $$m_1=-1$$ and $$\phi=120^\circ$$ where $$\tan120^\circ=-\sqrt3$$; solve for $$m_2$$ then line through $$P$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Let slope of $$l_2$$ be $$m.$$ Use $$\tan\phi=\frac{m-(-1)}{1+(-1)m}=\frac{m+1}{1-m}$$ (signed). For $$\phi=120^\circ,$$ $$\tan120^\circ=-\sqrt3,$$ so $$\frac{m+1}{1-m}=-\sqrt3\Rightarrow m+1=-\sqrt3+\sqrt3 m\Rightarrow m(1-\sqrt3)=-(1+\sqrt3)\Rightarrow m=\frac{1+\sqrt3}{\sqrt3-1}=2+\sqrt3.$$ The other line corresponds to $$\phi=60^\circ$$ (since obtuse 120° means acute 60° between directions): $$\tan60^\circ=\sqrt3,$$ so $$\frac{m+1}{1-m}=\sqrt3\Rightarrow m=2-\sqrt3.$$ Through $$P(2,2):$$ If $$m=2+\sqrt3,$$ $$y-2=(2+\sqrt3)(x-2).$$ If $$m=2-\sqrt3,$$ $$y-2=(2-\sqrt3)(x-2).$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: The line passes through $$(-1,6)$$ and makes an angle of $$25^\circ$$ with the positive $$x$$-axis. Find its equation (leave slope as $$\tan25^\circ$$).
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Slope is $$\tan25^\circ$$; use point–slope.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A ship travels on a bearing of $$060^\circ$$ (clockwise from North). On an $$xy$$-plane where $$x$$ is East and $$y$$ is North, the ship passes through $$P(2,1)$$. Find the equation of its path.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Bearing $$060^\circ$$ means angle from East axis is $$30^\circ$$ above +x; slope $$=\tan30^\circ=\frac1{\sqrt3}$$.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Direction makes angle $$30^\circ$$ with +x axis, so $$m=\tan30^\circ=\frac1{\sqrt3}.$$ Through $$P(2,1):$$ $$y-1=\frac{1}{\sqrt3}(x-2)\Rightarrow y=\frac{1}{\sqrt3}x+1-\frac{2}{\sqrt3}.$$

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_title: Angle with x-axis + through two points check
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: A line passes through $$A(0,-3)$$ and makes an angle of $$\theta$$ with the positive $$x$$-axis such that $$\sin\theta=\frac{3}{5}$$ and $$\theta$$ is acute. Find the equation.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: From $$\sin\theta=\frac35$$, get $$\cos\theta=\frac45$$, so $$\tan\theta=\frac{3/5}{4/5}=\frac34$$.

Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_title: Angle with x-axis + line through intersection
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.question_text: Lines $$x+y=6$$ and $$2x-y=1$$ meet at $$P$$. Find equation of the line through $$P$$ making angle $$45^\circ$$ with the positive $$x$$-axis.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.hint: Find $$P$$ first; then slope $$m=\tan45^\circ=1$$; use point–slope.
Chapter 5-Straight line graphs.solution_text: Solve: add equations after writing $$2x-y=1\Rightarrow y=2x-1.$$ Substitute into $$x+y=6:$$ $$x+2x-1=6\Rightarrow3x=7\Rightarrow x=\frac73,$$ $$y=\frac{14}{3}-1=\frac{11}{3}.$$ Through $$P\left(\frac73,\frac{11}{3}\right)$$ with $$m=1:$$ $$y-\frac{11}{3}=1\left(x-\frac73\right)\Rightarrow y=x+\frac{4}{3}.$$
